sentences.zh: 志七十七

translations.literal: Treatise 77
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 77

sentences.zh: 輿服一

translations.literal: Carriages and Dress 1
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Dress I

sentences.zh: 皇帝五輅皇帝輦輿皇后輿車皇太后輿車附皇貴妃以下輿車

translations.literal: The Emperor's Five Chariots; Imperial Palanquins and Litters; the Empress's Carriages; the Empress Dowager's Carriages; appended: carriages for Imperial Noble Consort and below
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's Five Chariots, Imperial Palanquins and Litters, the Empress's Carriages, the Empress Dowager's Carriages—with an appendix on carriages for the Imperial Noble Consort and those of lower rank

sentences.zh: 親王以下輿車親王福晉以下輿車京外職官輿車庶民附

translations.literal: Carriages for princes and below; carriages for princess consorts of princes and below; carriages for officials outside the capital; commoners, appended
translations.idiomatic: Carriages for Princes and Below, for Princess Consorts of Princes and Below, for Officials Outside the Capital, and Commoners (appendix)

sentences.zh: 命婦輿車

translations.literal: Carriages for titled women
translations.idiomatic: Carriages for Titled Women

sentences.zh: 自虞廷藻繢，制創垂衣。

translations.literal: From the patterned splendor of the Yu court, institutions were created and the draped-robe [ideal of rule] was established.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the court of Yu adorned itself in patterned brocade, ritual institutions took shape and the image of rule in flowing robes was fixed.

sentences.zh: 車服之朌，式昭庸典。

translations.literal: The apportionment of chariots and dress, in manner manifested the standard canon.
translations.idiomatic: How chariots and garments were allotted in turn made plain the enduring ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 夏絻殷輅，文質異觀。

translations.literal: The Xia had fine caps, the Yin had grand chariots; ornament and substance differed in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia favored fine ceremonial caps and the Shang grand chariots—each age paired refinement and plain substance in its own way.

sentences.zh: 迄乎有周，監於二代。

translations.literal: Down to the Zhou, they took the two previous dynasties as models.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhou, rulers looked back to the two preceding dynasties as their guide.

sentences.zh: 巾車典路，司服司常。

translations.literal: The Master of Chariots regulated the roads; the Director of Garments and the Director of Standards [each had charge].
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Chariots kept the roads in order, while the Directors of Garments and of Standards each held their own charge.

sentences.zh: 各隸專官，禮明物備。

translations.literal: Each was subordinate to a dedicated officer; ritual was clarified and implements made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Each fell under its own specialist officer, so that ritual was clear and every requisite object was in place.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以降，代有異同。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, each age had its differences and similarities.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin and Han onward, every dynasty had its own variations on the same theme.

sentences.zh: 品數彌繁，曩篇具載。

translations.literal: Grades and numbers grew ever more numerous; earlier treatises record them fully.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks and categories multiplied endlessly, and earlier chapters of this history record them in full.

sentences.zh: 明初木輅，乃用於郊，崇朴去雕，亦有足尚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, the wooden chariot was used at the suburban sacrifices; honoring simplicity and removing carving, this too is worthy of esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming the wooden chariot was used for suburban sacrifices—a preference for plainness over ornament that is itself admirable.

sentences.zh: 清之太祖，肇起東陲，遠略是勤，戎衣在御。

translations.literal: The Taizu of Qing, rising first in the eastern marches, was diligent in distant strategy, with martial garb ever on his person.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's founding Taizu rose in the eastern borderlands, pressing distant campaigns while still clad for war.

sentences.zh: 太宗纘服，遂定遼都。

translations.literal: Taizong succeeded to the throne and thereupon fixed the capital at Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took the throne and established the capital in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 天聰六年，已命禮官考定儀衛，並因易服蔑祖之弊，鑒及金、元。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiancong, he already ordered ritual officials to examine and fix ceremonial guards, and because of the abuse of changing dress and slighting ancestors, took warning from Jin and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: As early as the sixth year of Tiancong he ordered ritual officials to codify ceremonial guards, mindful of how the Jin and Yuan had erred by changing dress and forgetting their forebears.

sentences.zh: 國俗衣冠，一沿舊式。

translations.literal: National custom in caps and robes followed the old forms throughout.
translations.idiomatic: National dress and headgear kept to the old Manchu forms without exception.

sentences.zh: 勿忘數典，昭示雲礽。

translations.literal: Do not forget the many canons; make manifest to the descendants.
translations.idiomatic: They were not to forget the ancestral statutes, but to display them for generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，撫有中夏。

translations.literal: Shizu entered the Pass and pacified all China.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu crossed the Pass and brought the Central Realm under rule,

sentences.zh: 武功耆定，文物浸昌。

translations.literal: Martial achievements were settled in old age, and cultural institutions gradually flourished.
translations.idiomatic: military glory was secured and civil institutions steadily flourished.

sentences.zh: 康、雍兩朝，續有制作。

translations.literal: In the two reigns of Kangxi and Yongzheng, further creations followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi and Yongzheng reigns saw one new regulation after another.

sentences.zh: 朝章國采，斯已粲然。

translations.literal: Court regulations and national ritual already shone brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Court protocol and state ceremony had already taken luminous form.

sentences.zh: 亦越高宗，衣聞克紹。

translations.literal: Also surpassing Gaozong, the garment tradition was able to be continued.
translations.idiomatic: Even Gaozong of Tang was surpassed, for the ritual of dress could be carried on intact.

sentences.zh: 治承熙洽，鄉用儒臣。

translations.literal: Governance inherited a prosperous harmony; Confucian ministers were employed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Rule enjoyed an age of radiant peace, and Confucian scholars were called to serve in succession.

sentences.zh: 館辟三通，籀文緝。

translations.literal: Institutes were opened for the Three Comprehensive [Histories]; ancient script texts were compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Academies were founded for the great comprehensive histories, and archaic script texts were gathered and edited.

sentences.zh: 五輅之數，改符周官。

translations.literal: The number of five chariots was altered to accord with the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The five ceremonial chariots were renumbered to match the Zhou Offices.

sentences.zh: 參古准今，圖詳禮器。

translations.literal: Consulting antiquity and measuring the present, illustrated treatises detailed ritual implements.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars weighed antiquity against the present and produced illustrated compendia of ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 遂於乘御，增定已多。

translations.literal: Thereupon in riding and conveyance, additions and fixes were already many.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial transport alone saw a great many new specifications added.

sentences.zh: 一代儀文，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: The ceremonial institutions of a generation, at this point were at their fullest.
translations.idiomatic: Never had a single dynasty's ritual code reached such fullness as this.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，上下相承，率蹈前規，尚無侈改。

translations.literal: From that time onward, above and below succeeded one another, generally following former rules, and as yet without extravagant changes.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, court and country alike kept to precedent, and for the most part no one ventured extravagant revisions.

sentences.zh: 載稽諸制，爰志斯篇。

translations.literal: Examining all regulations, therefore this chapter is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Having reviewed the various regulations, we record them in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿一門，迾從附著。

translations.literal: The category of halberd guards and escorts is appended with the procession.
translations.idiomatic: The section on imperial halberd guards and escorts is treated in an appendix.

sentences.zh: 光、宣之際，海、陸軍興。

translations.literal: At the juncture of Guangxu and Xuantong, sea and land forces arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu and Xuantong era, modern navies and armies took shape.

sentences.zh: 旗式服章，舊觀頓改。

translations.literal: Banner patterns and dress insignia; the old appearance suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Flags, uniforms, and insignia changed overnight, and the old order vanished at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 已見兵志，茲不複書。

translations.literal: Already seen in the Military Treatises; here it is not written again.
translations.idiomatic: These matters are covered in the Military Treatises and are not repeated here.

sentences.zh: 璽、寶、印、符，所以昭信。

translations.literal: Seals, treasures, stamps, and tallies serve to manifest trust.
translations.idiomatic: Seals, imperial treasures, stamps, and tallies exist to authenticate authority.

sentences.zh: 龍、龜、蟲、鳥，紐篆各殊。

translations.literal: Dragon, tortoise, insect, and bird—knobs and seal script each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon, tortoise, insect, and bird motifs marked the knobs, and each rank had its own seal script.

sentences.zh: 列代相沿，皆資法守。

translations.literal: Successive dynasties transmitted them; all relied on statutory observance.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty handed them down, and all alike depended on fixed law.

sentences.zh: 備詳定式，悉按等差。

translations.literal: Fully detailing the fixed forms, all according to graded distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Their prescribed forms are set out in full, each grade observing its proper distinction.

sentences.zh: 又自海通，國交最重。

translations.literal: Moreover from the opening of sea communications, interstate relations were most weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Once maritime trade opened, diplomatic relations with foreign states became paramount.

sentences.zh: 往來酬贈，仿製寶星。

translations.literal: In coming and going, gifts were exchanged; treasured stars were imitated in manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Courtesies were exchanged in kind, and orders of merit were fashioned after foreign models.

sentences.zh: 名級攸分，以榮佩戴。

translations.literal: Names and grades were each divided, to honor those who wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and ranks were carefully distinguished, so that wearers might be honored accordingly.

sentences.zh: 逮乎末季，新制漸繁，兼有爵章，行之未久。

translations.literal: Reaching the final age, new systems gradually multiplied; there were also noble insignia, practiced not long.
translations.idiomatic: By the dynasty's end new insignia multiplied, including noble badges that had scarcely been in use.

sentences.zh: 若斯之類，隱略云爾。

translations.literal: Such categories as these are treated in brief summary only.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of that sort are passed over here in brief.

sentences.zh: 清初仍明舊，有玉輅、大輅、大馬輦、小馬輦之制，與香步輦並稱五輦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qing they still followed Ming usage: there were regulations for the jade chariot, great chariot, great horse palanquin, and small horse palanquin, which together with the fragrant step palanquin were called the five palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing still followed Ming practice: the jade chariot, great chariot, great and small horse palanquins, and the fragrant step palanquin were collectively known as the Five Palanquins.

sentences.zh: 大朝日設於太和門東。

translations.literal: On great court days they were set out east of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: On major court days they were displayed east of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 又涼步輦、大儀轎、大轎、明轎、折合明轎，均左所掌之。

translations.literal: Moreover the cool step palanquin, great ceremonial sedan, great sedan, bright sedan, and folding bright sedan were all managed by the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: The cool step palanquin, great ceremonial sedan, great sedan, bright sedan, and folding bright sedan were likewise under the Left Office's charge.

sentences.zh: 冬至大祀、夏至祀方澤、並乘涼步輦，升殿日亦設於太和門東。

translations.literal: For the great sacrifice at winter solstice and the summer solstice sacrifice at the Square Mound Altar, all rode the cool step palanquin; on days of ascending the hall they were also set east of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: For the winter-solstice grand sacrifice and the summer-solstice sacrifice at the Square Mound, the emperor rode the cool step palanquin, which on hall-audience days was also stationed east of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，定大祀親詣行禮，均乘輿出宮，至太和門乘輦。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong, it was fixed that for great sacrifices when the emperor went in person to perform the rites, all rode the litter out of the palace, and at the Gate of Supreme Harmony mounted the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7 it was decreed that for major sacrifices the emperor would leave the palace in a litter and transfer to a palanquin at the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 祀畢還宮，仍備輿。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was completed and they returned to the palace, litters were still provided.
translations.idiomatic: After the rite, litters were kept ready for the return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 八年，改大輅為金輅，大馬輦為象輅，小馬輦為革輅，香步輦為木輅，玉輅仍舊，是為五輅，鑾儀衛掌之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the great chariot was changed to the gold chariot, the great horse palanquin to the elephant chariot, the small horse palanquin to the leather chariot, the fragrant step palanquin to the wood chariot; the jade chariot remained as before—these were the five chariots, managed by the Imperial Procession Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 8 the great chariot became the gold chariot, the great horse palanquin the elephant chariot, the small horse palanquin the leather chariot, and the fragrant step palanquin the wood chariot, while the jade chariot was unchanged—these Five Chariots were entrusted to the Imperial Procession Guard.

sentences.zh: 遇大朝會，則陳於午門外。

translations.literal: When there was a great court assembly, they were displayed outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At grand court assemblies they were arrayed outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 十三年，諭定乘用五輅，自今歲南郊始。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict fixed the use of the five chariots, beginning with this year's southern suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 an edict mandated use of the Five Chariots, starting with that year's southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 更造玉輦，改涼步輦為金輦，是為二輦。

translations.literal: A new jade palanquin was built; the cool step palanquin was changed to the gold palanquin—these were the two palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: A new jade palanquin was built and the cool step palanquin redesignated the gold palanquin—the Two Palanquins.

sentences.zh: 又定大儀轎為禮輿，改折合明轎為輕步輿，定大轎為步輿，是為三輿。

translations.literal: Moreover the great ceremonial sedan was fixed as the ritual litter; the folding bright sedan was changed to the light step litter; the great sedan was fixed as the step litter—these were the three litters.
translations.idiomatic: The great ceremonial sedan became the ritual litter, the folding bright sedan the light step litter, and the great sedan the step litter—the Three Litters.

sentences.zh: 南郊乘玉輦，北郊、太廟、社稷壇，乘金輦，朝日、夕月、耕耤以下諸祀，均乘禮輿。

translations.literal: For the southern suburb one rode the jade palanquin; for the northern suburb, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altars of Soil and Grain, the gold palanquin; for the sunrise, sunset, ploughing, and the sacrifices below these, all rode the ritual litter.
translations.idiomatic: The jade palanquin served the southern suburb; the gold palanquin the northern suburb, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Altars of Soil and Grain; the ritual litter all lesser rites from the sun cults through the ploughing ceremony.

sentences.zh: 遇大朝會，則並陳於太和門外。

translations.literal: When there was a great court assembly, all were displayed together outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: At grand court assemblies all were displayed together outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 行幸御輕步輿，駕出入則御步輿。

translations.literal: On imperial tours one used the light step litter; on entering and leaving while driving, one used the step litter.
translations.idiomatic: On tours the emperor rode the light step litter; for ordinary departures and returns, the step litter.

sentences.zh: 皇子輿車，俟分封后始制。

translations.literal: Carriages for imperial sons were made only after enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons received their carriages only after enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 茲撮集禮器圖所載，其乾隆以前所定者為初制，依類附見，用備參稽。

translations.literal: Here is gathered what is recorded in the Illustrated Ritual Implements; what was fixed before Qianlong is treated as the initial system, appended by category for reference.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is drawn from the Illustrated Ritual Implements: regulations fixed before Qianlong are noted as the original system and appended by category for consultation.

sentences.zh: 皇帝玉輅，木質魨硃，圓蓋方軫，高一丈二尺一寸。

translations.literal: The Emperor's jade chariot: wooden, cinnabar-lacquered, round canopy and square frame, height one zhang two chi one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's jade chariot was of wood finished in cinnabar lacquer, with a round canopy atop a square frame, standing one zhang, two chi, and one cun high.

sentences.zh: 蓋高三尺一分，青飾，銜玉圓版四。

translations.literal: The canopy was three chi one cun high, green ornamentation, holding four jade round plaques.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy rose three chi and one cun, was trimmed in green, and bore four round jade plaques.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂一尺二寸九分，承以鏤金垂雲檐八尺一寸，貼鏤金雲版三層。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top one chi two cun nine fen, supported by openwork gilded hanging-cloud eaves eight chi one cun, with three layers of applied openwork gilded cloud panels.
translations.idiomatic: It was crowned by a gilded round cap one chi, two cun, and nine fen across, borne on openwork gilded cloud eaves eight chi and one cun long, with three tiers of gilded cloud panels applied beneath.

sentences.zh: 青緞垂幨亦三層，綉金雲龍羽文相間。

translations.literal: Green satin hanging curtains also in three layers, embroidered with gold clouds, dragons, and feather patterns alternating.
translations.idiomatic: Three tiers of green satin curtains hung below, embroidered alternately with golden clouds, dragons, and feather motifs.

sentences.zh: 系帶四，綉金青緞為之，屬於軫。

translations.literal: Four fastening bands, made of green satin embroidered in gold, attached to the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Four bands of gold-embroidered green satin were fastened to the frame.

sentences.zh: 四柱高六尺七寸九分，相距各五尺六寸，繪金雲龍。

translations.literal: Four pillars, height six chi seven cun nine fen, each spaced five chi six cun apart, painted with gold clouds and dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each six chi, seven cun, and nine fen tall and five chi six cun apart, were painted with golden clouds and dragons.

sentences.zh: 門垂硃簾，四面各三。

translations.literal: At the doors hung vermilion curtains, three on each of the four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion curtains hung at each door, three to every side.

sentences.zh: 座縱八尺五寸，橫八尺四寸，環以硃闌，飾間金彩。

translations.literal: The seat was eight chi five cun long and eight chi four cun wide, encircled by vermilion rails ornamented with inset gold coloring.
translations.idiomatic: The platform measured eight chi five cun by eight chi four cun and was ringed by vermilion rails inlaid with gold.

sentences.zh: 闌內周布花毯。

translations.literal: Within the rails floral carpets were spread all around.
translations.idiomatic: Floral carpets were laid around the interior within the rails.

sentences.zh: 雲龍寶座在中，高一尺三寸，闊二尺九寸。

translations.literal: In the center was the cloud-dragon throne, one chi three cun high and two chi nine cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: At the center stood the cloud-and-dragon throne, one chi three cun high and two chi nine cun wide.

sentences.zh: 兩輪各十有八輻，鏤花飾金。

translations.literal: The two wheels each had eighteen spokes, openwork floral design with gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the two wheels had eighteen openwork spokes finished in gold.

sentences.zh: 貫以軸轅二，長二丈二尺九寸五分，金龍首尾飾兩端。

translations.literal: Pierced by two axles and shafts, length two zhang two chi nine cun five fen, with gilded dragon heads and tails ornamenting both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Two axles and shafts, two zhang, two chi, nine cun, and five fen long, passed through the wheels, their ends capped with gilded dragon heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 軫長一丈一尺一寸五分，徑八尺四寸。

translations.literal: The frame was one zhang one chi one cun five fen long, diameter eight chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: The square frame measured one zhang, one chi, one cun, and five fen on a side, with an overall width of eight chi four cun.

sentences.zh: 後建太常，十二斿，亦青緞為之，繰綉日月五星，斿綉二十八宿，里俱綉金龍，下垂五彩流蘇。

translations.literal: Behind was erected the Grand Constant, twelve pennants, also of green satin; the cords embroidered with sun, moon, and five stars; the pennants embroidered with the twenty-eight lodges; the lining all embroidered with gold dragons; hanging down were five-colored tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Behind rose the Grand Constant banner with twelve pennants of green satin: its cords bore the sun, moon, and five planets; each pennant the twenty-eight lunar mansions; the lining golden dragons throughout; and five-colored tassels hung below.

sentences.zh: 用攢竹魨硃竿，左加闟戟，右飾龍首，並綴硃旄五，垂青緌。

translations.literal: Used was a bundled-bamboo cinnabar-lacquered pole; on the left was added a halberd-gate, on the right ornamented with a dragon head; also attached were five vermilion pennants, hanging green tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Its pole was bundled bamboo lacquered cinnabar red, with a halberd fitting on the left and a dragon head on the right, five vermilion pennants attached, and green tassels hanging down.

sentences.zh: 升用納陛五級，左右闌皆魨硃金彩。

translations.literal: To ascend, five steps of recessed tread were used; left and right rails were all cinnabar-lacquered with gold coloring.
translations.idiomatic: Five recessed steps served for mounting; the rails on either side were cinnabar lacquer with gold trim.

sentences.zh: 駕象一，靷以硃絨紃。

translations.literal: Drawn by one elephant, the traces of vermilion velvet cord.
translations.idiomatic: A single elephant drew it, harnessed with vermilion velvet traces.

sentences.zh: 陳設時，行馬二承轅，亦魨硃直竿，兩端俱鑽銅。

translations.literal: When displayed, two walking horses supported the shafts, also cinnabar-lacquered straight poles, both ends drilled with copper.
translations.idiomatic: When on display, two ceremonial horses supported the shafts on straight cinnabar-lacquered poles tipped with copper at both ends.

sentences.zh: 初制，玉輅尺寸與大輅同。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the jade chariot's dimensions were the same as the great chariot's.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original regulations the jade chariot matched the great chariot in size.

sentences.zh: 輅上平盤、滴珠板、輪輻、輪輞、車心、軸首、及駕轅諸索制並同。

translations.literal: The chariot's upper flat plate, pearl-drip board, wheel spokes, wheel rims, wheel hub, axle ends, and all harness-shaft cord regulations were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The upper platform, pearl-drip board, spokes, rims, hub, axle caps, and all harness cords matched the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 惟無平盤下十有二槅及左右八槅之飾。

translations.literal: Only it lacked the twelve lattice panels below the flat plate and the eight lattice panels left and right in ornament.
translations.idiomatic: It lacked only the twelve lattice panels beneath the platform and the eight side panels that adorned the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 輅亭前二柱，飾瀝粉貼金升龍，亭柱檻座尺寸，及門槅明栨裝飾與亭內軟座下諸制，悉同大輅。

translations.literal: The chariot pavilion's front two pillars were ornamented with gilded ascending dragons in liquid-gold powder; pavilion pillar, railing, and seat dimensions, and door lattice, bright leaf, and decoration with the soft seat below inside the pavilion—all regulations were the same as the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The two front pillars of the chariot pavilion bore ascending dragons in gilded powder; pillar, railing, and seat dimensions, door lattices, panels, and the cushioned seat within all followed the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 惟屏風上雕沈香色描金雲龍五，屏後下三槅雕木沈香色描金雲龍三，下雕雲板如其數，較大輅之制少異焉。

translations.literal: Only on the screen above were carved five agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragons; behind the screen the lower three lattice panels carved wood agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragons three; below carved cloud panels in corresponding number—somewhat differing from the great chariot's system.
translations.idiomatic: Only the screen differed slightly: five agarwood-toned, gold-traced cloud-dragons above; three on the three lattice panels behind; and cloud panels below in matching number—modest variations from the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 輅頂、圓盤、天輪、輅亭前諸制，及太常旗、踏梯、行馬之類，皆與大輅同。

translations.literal: The chariot top, round plate, heaven wheel, and all regulations before the chariot pavilion, and the Grand Constant banner, mounting ladder, walking horses, and the like—all were the same as the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy top, round plate, celestial wheel, pavilion fittings, Grand Constant banner, mounting ladder, and walking horses all matched the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 金輅，亦駕象一。

translations.literal: The gold chariot also was drawn by one elephant.
translations.idiomatic: The gold chariot, too, was drawn by a single elephant.

sentences.zh: 圓蓋方軫，黃飾，銜金圓版四。

translations.literal: Round canopy and square frame, yellow ornamentation, holding four gold round plaques.
translations.idiomatic: It had a round canopy and square frame in yellow trim, bearing four round gold plaques.

sentences.zh: 黃緞垂幨三層。

translations.literal: Three layers of yellow satin hanging curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Three tiers of yellow satin curtains hung below.

sentences.zh: 系帶四，亦黃緞為之，屬於軫。

translations.literal: Four fastening bands, also made of yellow satin, attached to the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Four bands of yellow satin were fastened to the frame.

sentences.zh: 後建大旗，十有二斿，各綉金龍。

translations.literal: Behind was erected a great banner, twelve pennants, each embroidered with a gold dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Behind rose a great banner with twelve pennants, each embroidered with a golden dragon.

sentences.zh: 餘如玉輅之制。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the jade chariot's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: All other features followed the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 按金輅之名，改由大輅。

translations.literal: As for the name gold chariot, it was changed from the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The gold chariot took its name when the great chariot was redesignated.

sentences.zh: 初制，大輅高一丈三尺九寸五分，廣八尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the great chariot was one zhang three chi nine cun five fen high, eight chi two cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the great chariot stood one zhang, three chi, nine cun, and five fen high and eight chi, two cun, and five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 輅上平盤，前後車欞並雁翅及四垂如意。

translations.literal: On the chariot's upper flat plate, front and rear carriage rails together with goose-wing [extensions] and four hanging ruyi [ornaments].
translations.idiomatic: Its upper platform bore front and rear rails, goose-wing extensions, and four hanging ruyi ornaments.

sentences.zh: 滴珠板下二轅，各長二丈二尺九寸有奇，俱硃魨鍍金銅龍首尾，鱗葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Below the pearl-drip board were two shafts, each more than two zhang two chi nine cun long, all cinnabar-lacquered with gilded copper dragon heads and tails, scale-leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the pearl-drip board two shafts, each over two zhang, two chi, and nine cun long, were lacquered cinnabar and capped with gilded copper dragon heads and tails set with scale-shaped plates.

sentences.zh: 平盤下方箱，四周硃魨匡，前後十二槅，內青地繪五彩雲鶴，左右八槅，內上青下綠地，繪獸鳥各六。

translations.literal: Below the flat plate was the lower box, on four sides cinnabar-lacquered frames; front and rear twelve lattice panels, inside green ground painted with five-colored clouds and cranes; left and right eight lattice panels, inside upper green lower green ground, painted six each of beasts and birds.
translations.idiomatic: Below the platform sat the lower box framed in cinnabar lacquer: twelve lattice panels fore and aft on a blue ground painted with five-colored clouds and cranes; eight side panels, blue above and green below, each bearing six beasts and six birds.

sentences.zh: 輪二，貫以軸，每輪十八輻輞，皆硃魨，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Two wheels, pierced by an axle; each wheel eighteen spokes and rims, all cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Two wheels on a shared axle, each with eighteen cinnabar-lacquered spokes and rims studded with gilded copper floral plates.

sentences.zh: 輪內車心各一，抹金銅鈒蓮花瓣輪盤裝釘。

translations.literal: Within each wheel one hub, gilded copper inlaid lotus-petal wheel disks nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Each wheel had a hub faced with gilded copper lotus-petal disks.

sentences.zh: 軸首左右鐵插貫之，抹金銅鈒龍頂管心裝釘。

translations.literal: At the axle ends left and right iron plugs pierced through; gilded copper inlaid dragon-cap tube centers nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Iron pins passed through the axle ends, capped with gilded copper dragon-head tube fittings.

sentences.zh: 軸中纏紅絨駕轅諸索。

translations.literal: At the axle center were wound red-velvet harness-shaft cords and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Red velvet harness cords were wound about the axle center.

sentences.zh: 輅亭高六尺七寸九分，四柱各長五尺八寸四分。

translations.literal: The chariot pavilion was six chi seven cun nine fen high; the four pillars each five chi eight cun four fen long.
translations.idiomatic: The chariot pavilion stood six chi, seven cun, and nine fen high, with four pillars each five chi, eight cun, and four fen long.

sentences.zh: 檻座高九寸五分，前後柱戧金雲龍文，下山水。

translations.literal: The railing seat was nine cun five fen high; front and rear pillars bore gilded cloud-dragon patterns, with landscapes below.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base rose nine cun and five fen; front and rear pillars showed gilded cloud-dragons above landscapes below.

sentences.zh: 門高五尺一寸九分，廣二尺四寸九分。

translations.literal: The door was five chi one cun nine fen high and two chi four cun nine fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Each door measured five chi, one cun, and nine fen high by two chi, four cun, and nine fen wide.

sentences.zh: 左右門各廣二尺二寸五分，上四周裝雕木沈香色描金香草板十二片。

translations.literal: The left and right doors were each two chi two cun five fen wide; above on four sides were mounted twelve carved agarwood-colored gold-traced vanilla-pattern panels.
translations.idiomatic: Side doors were two chi, two cun, and five fen wide, with twelve agarwood-toned, gold-traced floral panels set around the upper frame.

sentences.zh: 前左右各有槅二扇，明栨全，皆硃魨，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Front left and right each had two lattice-panel leaves, bright panels complete, all cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Fore and aft on each side stood two cinnabar-lacquered lattice doors with bright panels, all studded with gilded copper floral plates.

sentences.zh: 槅編黃線絛，後硃魨屏風，屏前上三槅，雕沈香色描金雲龍五。

translations.literal: The lattice was woven with yellow cord tassels; behind was a cinnabar-lacquered screen; before the screen the upper three lattice panels carved five agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Lattice panels were bound with yellow cord; behind them a cinnabar screen bore five agarwood-toned, gold-traced dragons on its upper panels.

sentences.zh: 上硃魨板，戧金雲龍一。

translations.literal: Above, a cinnabar-lacquered panel with one gilded cloud-dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Above it sat a cinnabar panel with a single gilded cloud-dragon.

sentences.zh: 中三槅，沈香色描金雲龍三。

translations.literal: The middle three lattice panels: three agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The middle three panels bore three agarwood-toned, gold-traced cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 下三槅，描金雲板如其數。

translations.literal: The lower three lattice panels: gold-traced cloud panels in corresponding number.
translations.idiomatic: The lower three panels had matching gold-traced cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 屏後上三槅，硃魨戧金龍三。

translations.literal: Behind the screen the upper three lattice panels: three cinnabar-lacquered gilded dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the screen, the upper three panels showed three cinnabar dragons in gold.

sentences.zh: 其次戧金雲板如其數。

translations.literal: Next, gilded cloud panels in corresponding number.
translations.idiomatic: Below them came matching gilded cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 中三槅，硃魨戧金龍四。

translations.literal: The middle three lattice panels: four cinnabar-lacquered gilded dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The middle three panels bore four cinnabar dragons in gold.

sentences.zh: 其次沈香色描金雲板如其數。

translations.literal: Next, agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud panels in corresponding number.
translations.idiomatic: Next came agarwood-toned, gold-traced cloud panels in matching number.

sentences.zh: 下三槅，沈香色雲板亦如之。

translations.literal: The lower three lattice panels: agarwood-colored cloud panels likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The lower three panels had agarwood-toned cloud panels to match.

sentences.zh: 俱抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: All with gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: All were studded with gilded copper floral plates.

sentences.zh: 亭內黃線絛編硃魨匡，軟座黃絨墜座大索四，下垂蓮花墜石，上施花毯草席，並大紅織金綺褥。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion yellow cord tassels wove a cinnabar-lacquered frame; the soft seat had four great yellow-velvet hanging cords with lotus pendants and stones below; floral carpets, rush mats, and great red brocaded gold cushions were laid on top.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, yellow cord framed a cinnabar border around a soft seat with four yellow-velvet cords bearing lotus pendants and stones, covered by floral carpets, rush mats, and red brocaded gold cushions.

sentences.zh: 硃魨坐椅一，上靠背雕沈香色描金雲龍一，下雕雲板一，硃魨福壽板一，並衣黃織金椅靠、坐褥、四圍椅裙全。

translations.literal: One cinnabar-lacquered chair: above the backrest one carved agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragon; below one carved cloud panel; one cinnabar fortune-longevity panel; with yellow brocaded gold chair back, seat cushion, and four-sided chair skirt complete.
translations.idiomatic: A cinnabar chair bore one agarwood-toned, gold-traced dragon on its back, a cloud panel below, and a fortune-longevity panel, with yellow brocaded gold back, cushion, and skirt complete.

sentences.zh: 周圍施黃綾帷幔，或用黃線羅。

translations.literal: All around were hung yellow gauze curtains, or yellow cord gauze might be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow gauze curtains encircled the pavilion, though yellow cord gauze might be used instead.

sentences.zh: 亭外青綺緣邊紅簾十扇，各用拽簾黃線絛二，黃銅圈全。

translations.literal: Outside the pavilion, ten red curtains with green brocade borders; each used two yellow cord tassels for drawing the curtain, with brass rings complete.
translations.idiomatic: Outside hung ten red curtains edged in green brocade, each with two yellow draw-cords and brass rings.

sentences.zh: 輅頂並圓盤高三尺一分，鍍金銅蹲龍頂，帶仰覆蓮座，高一尺二寸九分垂攀頂黃絨索四。

translations.literal: The chariot top together with the round plate was three chi one cun high; a gilded copper crouching-dragon top, with inverted lotus seat, one chi two cun nine fen high; four yellow-velvet cords hung from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy and round plate together rose three chi and one cun, crowned by a gilded copper crouching dragon on a lotus base one chi, two cun, and nine fen high, with four yellow velvet cords from the apex.

sentences.zh: 盤高二寸，上加硃魨。

translations.literal: The plate was two cun high, with cinnabar lacquer added above.
translations.idiomatic: The plate rose two cun, lacquered cinnabar above.

sentences.zh: 其下外四面沈香色地，描金雲青飾。

translations.literal: Below it on the outer four sides was an agarwood-colored ground with gold-traced clouds and green ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Its outer faces were agarwood-toned, traced in gold clouds with green trim.

sentences.zh: 輅蓋亭內貼金斗拱，承硃魨匡寶蓋，斗以八頂，黃綺冒之，名曰黃屋。

translations.literal: Within the chariot canopy pavilion were gilded bracket sets supporting a cinnabar-lacquered treasured canopy; eight bracket arms, covered with yellow brocade—called the Yellow Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the canopy, gilded brackets bore a cinnabar treasured canopy on eight arms, veiled in yellow brocade—the Yellow Canopy.

sentences.zh: 中並四周綉五彩雲龍九。

translations.literal: In the center and on four sides were embroidered nine five-colored cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Center and four sides bore nine five-colored embroidered cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 天輪三層，硃魨，上安雕木貼金龍耀葉板八十一片。

translations.literal: The heaven wheel in three layers, cinnabar-lacquered, above mounted eighty-one carved wood gilded dragon radiant leaf panels.
translations.idiomatic: Three cinnabar heaven-wheel tiers carried eighty-one gilded dragon-and-leaf panels.

sentences.zh: 三層間繪五彩雲，襯板數亦如之。

translations.literal: Between the three layers were painted five-colored clouds; the lining panels were equal in number.
translations.idiomatic: Five-colored clouds painted the spaces between tiers, with matching lining panels.

sentences.zh: 盤下四周黃銅裝釘，上施金黃綺瀝水三層，每層摺片八十有一，間綉五彩雲龍文。

translations.literal: Below the plate on four sides were brass fittings; above were three layers of golden-yellow brocade eaves-drip, each layer eighty-one folded pieces, between them embroidered five-colored cloud-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Brass fittings ringed the plate below; above hung three tiers of golden brocade eaves, eighty-one folds each, embroidered with five-colored cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 四角垂青綺絡帶，各綉五彩雲升龍三。

translations.literal: At the four corners hung green brocade net bands, each embroidered with three five-colored cloud ascending-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Green brocade net bands at each corner bore three five-colored ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 圓盤四角連輅座板用攀頂黃線圓絛，並貼金木魚。

translations.literal: At the four corners of the round plate, connecting to the chariot seat boards, yellow cord round tassels for the climbing top, and gilded wood fish.
translations.idiomatic: Round plate corners linked to the seat with yellow climbing cords and gilded wooden fish.

sentences.zh: 輅亭前有左右轉角闌干二扇，後一字帶左右轉角闌干一扇，皆硃魨。

translations.literal: Before the chariot pavilion were left and right corner-turning railings two panels; behind, one straight panel with left and right corner-turning railings—all cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the pavilion stood two corner rail panels to left and right; behind, one straight panel with corner rails—all cinnabar red.

sentences.zh: 內嵌雕木貼金龍，間以五彩雲。

translations.literal: Inlaid carved wood gilded dragons, interspersed with five-colored clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Inlaid gilded dragons alternated with five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 三扇凡十二柱，各柱首雕木貼金蹲龍一，及描金五彩裝蓮花抱柱。

translations.literal: The three panels totaled twelve pillars; each pillar top had one carved wood gilded crouching dragon, and five-colored gilded lotus pillar-caps.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pillars on three panels each bore a gilded crouching dragon and five-colored lotus cap.

sentences.zh: 闌內四周施花毯草席。

translations.literal: Within the rails floral carpets and rush mats were spread all around.
translations.idiomatic: Floral carpets and rush mats lined the interior rails.

sentences.zh: 其後樹太常旗二，黃雲緞為之，皆十有二斿。

translations.literal: Behind were erected two Grand Constant banners, of yellow cloud satin, each with twelve pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Behind rose two Grand Constant banners of yellow cloud satin, each with twelve pennants.

sentences.zh: 每斿內外各綉升龍一。

translations.literal: Within each pennant inside and outside was embroidered one ascending dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Each pennant bore an ascending dragon inside and out.

sentences.zh: 硃魨攢竹竿二，左竿旗腰綉日月北斗，竿首用鍍金銅龍頭。

translations.literal: Two cinnabar-lacquered bundled-bamboo poles; the left pole banner waist embroidered sun, moon, and Northern Dipper; the pole top used a gilded copper dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: Two cinnabar bamboo poles: the left banner showed sun, moon, and Big Dipper at the waist, with a gilded dragon head atop.

sentences.zh: 右竿旗腰綉黻字，竿首用鍍金銅戟。

translations.literal: The right pole banner waist embroidered the fu character; the pole top used a gilded copper halberd.
translations.idiomatic: The right banner bore the fu character at the waist, capped with a gilded halberd.

sentences.zh: 各綴抹金銅鈴二，垂紅纓十有二，上施抹金銅寶蓋，下垂青線帉。

translations.literal: Each attached two gilded copper bells, hanging twelve red tassels; above was a gilded copper treasured canopy, hanging green cord pendants below.
translations.idiomatic: Each pole bore two gilded bells, twelve red tassels, a gilded canopy, and green cord pendants below.

sentences.zh: 踏梯一，木質硃魨，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: One mounting ladder, wooden cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: One cinnabar mounting ladder studded with gilded copper floral plates.

sentences.zh: 行馬架二，木質硃魨，抹金銅葉片裝釘，上穿黃絨匾絛。

translations.literal: Two walking-horse frames, wooden cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper leaf pieces nailed on, pierced with yellow velvet tablet cords above.
translations.idiomatic: Two cinnabar walking-horse frames, gilded and pierced with yellow velvet cords.

sentences.zh: 黃布面絹里夾幰衣、油綢雨衣各一，紅油合扇梯、紅油拓叉各一。

translations.literal: One each of yellow-cloth-faced silk-lined canopy coat and oiled-silk raincoat; one each of red-oiled folding ladder and red-oiled support fork.
translations.idiomatic: It carried a yellow canopy coat, oiled-silk raincoat, red-oiled folding ladder, and red-oiled support fork.

sentences.zh: 貼金銅寶瓶，並木雕貼金仰覆蓮座，雕花番草貼金象鞍、鞦轡、氈籠各二副。

translations.literal: Gilded copper treasured vases, and carved wood gilded inverted lotus seats, carved floral scroll gilded elephant saddles, bridles, and felt covers—two sets each.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded treasured vases, lotus seats, saddles, bridles, and felt covers came in two sets each.

sentences.zh: 象輅，服馬四，驂馬六，設游環和鈴，圓蓋方軫。

translations.literal: The elephant chariot: four harness horses, six outrider horses, with swinging rings and harmony bells; round canopy and square frame.
translations.idiomatic: The elephant chariot used four harness horses and six outriders, with harmony bells, a round canopy, and square frame.

sentences.zh: 高一丈一尺三寸，蓋高二尺六寸五分，紅飾銜象牙圓版四。

translations.literal: Height one zhang one chi three cun; canopy two chi six cun five fen high; red ornamentation holding four ivory round plaques.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one zhang, one chi, and three cun high; the canopy two chi, six cun, and five fen, in red trim with four ivory round plaques.

sentences.zh: 紅緞垂幨三層，系帶四，亦紅緞為之，屬於軫。

translations.literal: Three layers of red satin hanging curtains; four fastening bands, also of red satin, attached to the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Three tiers of red satin curtains hung below, with four red satin bands on the frame.

sentences.zh: 四柱高六尺四寸九分，相距各五尺八寸。

translations.literal: Four pillars six chi four cun nine fen high, each spaced five chi eight cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each six chi, four cun, and nine fen tall, stood five chi eight cun apart.

sentences.zh: 座縱一丈五分，橫九尺一寸，環以硃闌。

translations.literal: The seat one zhang five cun long and nine chi one cun wide, encircled by vermilion rails.
translations.idiomatic: The platform measured one zhang and five cun by nine chi and one cun, ringed in vermilion rails.

sentences.zh: 轅三，各長二丈二尺三寸，軫長一丈五分，徑九尺一寸。

translations.literal: Three shafts, each two zhang two chi three cun long; frame one zhang five cun long, diameter nine chi one cun.
translations.idiomatic: Three shafts, each two zhang, two chi, and three cun long, joined a frame one zhang five cun wide and nine chi one cun across.

sentences.zh: 後建大赤，十有二斿，各綉金鳳。

translations.literal: Behind was erected the Great Scarlet, twelve pennants, each embroidered with a gold phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Behind rose the Great Scarlet banner with twelve pennants, each bearing a golden phoenix.

sentences.zh: 餘制與玉輅同。

translations.literal: The remaining regulations were the same as the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: All other features matched the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 按象輅為大馬輦之改定。

translations.literal: As for the elephant chariot name, it was changed from the great horse palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The elephant chariot was redesignated from the great horse palanquin.

sentences.zh: 初制，大馬輦高一丈二尺五寸九分，廣八尺九寸五分。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the great horse palanquin was one zhang two chi five cun nine fen high, eight chi nine cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the great horse palanquin stood one zhang, two chi, five cun, and nine fen high and eight chi, nine cun, and five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 轅二，各長二丈五寸九分。

translations.literal: Two shafts, each two zhang five cun nine fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Two shafts, each two zhang, five cun, and nine fen long.

sentences.zh: 輦上平盤、滴珠板、輪輻、輪輞、車心、軸首及駕轅諸索制，並如大輅。

translations.literal: The palanquin upper flat plate, pearl-drip board, spokes, rims, hub, axle ends, and harness-shaft cord regulations were all like the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Its platform, pearl-drip board, wheels, axles, and harness matched the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 亦無平盤下前後十二槅及左右八槅之飾。

translations.literal: Also lacking the twelve lattice panels below the flat plate front and rear and the eight lattice panels left and right in ornament.
translations.idiomatic: It likewise lacked the twelve fore-and-aft and eight side lattice panels of the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高六尺四寸九分，硃魨。

translations.literal: The palanquin pavilion six chi four cun nine fen high, cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion stood six chi, four cun, and nine fen high, in cinnabar lacquer.

sentences.zh: 四柱長五尺五寸四分。

translations.literal: The four pillars five chi five cun four fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each five chi, five cun, and four fen long.

sentences.zh: 檻座高如輦亭，上四周雕木沈香色描金雲板十二片，下亦如之。

translations.literal: The railing seat as high as the palanquin pavilion; above on four sides twelve carved agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud panels; below likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The railing matched the pavilion height, with twelve agarwood-toned cloud panels above and below.

sentences.zh: 門高五尺九分，廣二尺四寸五分。

translations.literal: The door five chi nine fen high, two chi four cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors measured five chi and nine fen high by two chi, four cun, and five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 左右門廣較減二寸。

translations.literal: The left and right doors were two cun narrower in width.
translations.idiomatic: Side doors were two cun narrower.

sentences.zh: 前及左右各有槅二扇，後槅三扇，明栨全，皆硃魨，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Front and left and right each had two lattice-panel leaves; rear three lattice-panel leaves; bright panels complete, all cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Front and sides had two lattice doors each, the rear three—all cinnabar, studded with gilded floral plates.

sentences.zh: 槅心編黃線絛。

translations.literal: The lattice centers were woven with yellow cord tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Lattice centers were bound with yellow cord.

sentences.zh: 亭內軟座，上施素毯。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion a soft seat, with plain mats laid on top.
translations.idiomatic: Inside was a soft seat covered with plain mats.

sentences.zh: 餘制與大輅同。

translations.literal: The remaining regulations were the same as the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: All else followed the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 輦頂並圓盤高二尺六寸五分，上下皆硃魨。

translations.literal: The palanquin top together with the round plate two chi six cun five fen high; above and below all cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy and round plate together rose two chi, six cun, and five fen, lacquered cinnabar throughout.

sentences.zh: 輦蓋青飾，銅龍、蓮座、寶蓋、黃屋諸制悉如大輅。

translations.literal: The palanquin canopy green ornamentation; copper dragon, lotus seat, treasured canopy, Yellow Canopy regulations all like the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Green canopy trim, copper dragon, lotus seat, treasured canopy, and Yellow Canopy all matched the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 天輪三層亦如之。

translations.literal: The heaven wheel three layers were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The three-tier heaven wheel did likewise.

sentences.zh: 輦亭前一字闌干一扇，後一字帶轉角闌干一扇，左右闌干二扇，內嵌絛環板，亦皆硃魨。

translations.literal: Before the palanquin pavilion one straight railing panel; behind one straight panel with corner-turning railings; left and right railings two panels; inlaid ring panels inside, also all cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the pavilion one straight rail; behind one with corner rails; two side rails—all cinnabar, with inlaid ring panels.

sentences.zh: 四扇凡十有二柱，各柱首雕飾同大輅。

translations.literal: The four panels totaled twelve pillars; each pillar-top ornament the same as the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Four panels held twelve pillars with caps matching the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 闌內周布素毯草席，太常旗、踏梯、行馬、幰衣、雨衣之類亦如之。

translations.literal: Within the rails plain mats and rush mats spread around; Grand Constant banner, mounting ladder, walking horses, canopy coat, raincoat, and the like were also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Plain mats and rush mats lined the rails; banners, ladder, horses, coats, and rain gear matched as well.

sentences.zh: 惟輅以象駕，輦以馬駕，故鞍韉、鞦轡、鈴纓之飾均備焉。

translations.literal: Only the chariot was drawn by elephants and the palanquin by horses; therefore saddle, bridle, bell, and tassel ornaments were all provided.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots used elephants and palanquins horses, so saddles, bridles, bells, and tassels were all provided.

sentences.zh: 木輅，服馬二，驂馬四，設游環和鈴，圓蓋方軫。

translations.literal: The wood chariot: two harness horses, four outrider horses, with swinging rings and harmony bells; round canopy and square frame.
translations.idiomatic: The wood chariot had two harness horses and four outriders, with harmony bells, a round canopy, and square frame.

sentences.zh: 高一丈一尺六寸五分，蓋高三尺六寸一分，黑飾銜花梨圓版四。

translations.literal: Height one zhang one chi six cun five fen; canopy three chi six cun one fen high; black ornamentation holding four pearwood round plaques.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one zhang, one chi, six cun, and five fen high; the canopy three chi, six cun, and one fen, in black with four pearwood plaques.

sentences.zh: 黑緞垂幨三層，系帶四，亦黑緞為之，屬於軫。

translations.literal: Three layers of black satin hanging curtains; four fastening bands, also of black satin, attached to the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Three tiers of black satin curtains and four black satin bands adorned the frame.

sentences.zh: 四柱高六尺五分，相距各五尺一寸。

translations.literal: Four pillars six chi five fen high, each spaced five chi one cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each six chi and five fen tall, stood five chi one cun apart.

sentences.zh: 座縱九尺，橫八尺八寸，環以硃闌。

translations.literal: The seat nine chi long and eight chi eight cun wide, encircled by vermilion rails.
translations.idiomatic: The platform measured nine chi by eight chi eight cun, ringed in vermilion rails.

sentences.zh: 轅三，各長二丈一尺。

translations.literal: Three shafts, each two zhang one chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Three shafts, each two zhang and one chi long.

sentences.zh: 軫長九尺，徑八尺八寸，後建大麾，十有二斿，各綉神武，餘俱如玉輅之制。

translations.literal: The frame nine chi long, diameter eight chi eight cun; behind was erected the Great Banner, twelve pennants, each embroidered with Divine Martial; the remainder all like the jade chariot regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The frame was nine chi long and eight chi eight cun wide; behind rose the Great Banner with twelve pennants embroidered with Divine Martial; all else matched the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 按木輅為香步輦之改制。

translations.literal: As for the wood chariot name, it was reformed from the fragrant step palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The wood chariot was redesignated from the fragrant step palanquin.

sentences.zh: 初制，香步輦高一丈二尺五寸，座高三尺，方廣八尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the fragrant step palanquin was one zhang two chi five cun high; the seat three chi high, square eight chi two cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the fragrant step palanquin stood one zhang, two chi, and five cun high, its seat three chi high and eight chi, two cun, and five fen square.

sentences.zh: 輦座硃魨，四周雕木五彩雲渾貼金龍板十二片，間以渾貼金仰覆蓮座，下雕木線金五彩雲板二十片。

translations.literal: The palanquin seat cinnabar-lacquered; on four sides twelve carved wood five-colored cloud wholly gilded dragon panels, interspersed with wholly gilded inverted lotus seats; below twenty carved wood line-gold five-colored cloud panels.
translations.idiomatic: Its cinnabar seat bore twelve wholly gilded dragon panels in five-colored clouds, lotus seats between, and twenty gilded cloud panels below.

sentences.zh: 座下四轅，中二轅長三丈五尺九寸，左右轅長二丈九尺五寸有奇，皆硃魨，鍍金銅龍首尾裝釘，攀轅黃線圓絛八。

translations.literal: Below the seat four shafts; the middle two shafts three zhang five chi nine cun long, left and right shafts more than two zhang nine chi five cun long, all cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper dragon heads and tails nailed on; eight yellow cord round tassels for pulling the shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Four shafts below: center pair three zhang, five chi, nine cun; side pair over two zhang, nine chi, five cun—all cinnabar, with gilded dragon caps and eight yellow pulling cords.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高六尺五分，四柱各長五尺八寸。

translations.literal: The palanquin pavilion six chi five fen high; the four pillars each five chi eight cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion stood six chi and five fen high on pillars five chi eight cun tall.

sentences.zh: 檻高二寸五分，亦皆硃魨，上四周雕木沈香色描金香草板十二片，抹金銅輅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: The railing two cun five fen high, also all cinnabar-lacquered; above on four sides twelve carved agarwood-colored gold-traced vanilla panels, gilded copper chariot inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: A cinnabar railing two cun five fen high bore twelve agarwood-toned floral panels, studded with gilded plates.

sentences.zh: 門較大馬輦高逾二寸，廣與之同。

translations.literal: The door more than two cun higher than the great horse palanquin; width the same.
translations.idiomatic: Doors stood two cun higher than the great horse palanquin but equally wide.

sentences.zh: 左右門廣二尺二寸。

translations.literal: The left and right doors two chi two cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Side doors were two chi and two cun wide.

sentences.zh: 前左右各硃魨十字槅二扇，雕沈香色描金雲龍板八片，下雲板如其數，俱抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Front left and right each two cinnabar-lacquered cross lattice-panel leaves; eight carved agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragon panels; cloud panels below in corresponding number; all gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Fore and side doors were cinnabar cross-lattice panels with eight agarwood-toned dragons and matching cloud panels, all gilded.

sentences.zh: 亭內布花毯草席，大紅織金綺褥，硃魨戧金龍坐椅一。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion floral carpets and rush mats spread; great red brocaded gold cushions; one cinnabar-lacquered gilded dragon chair.
translations.idiomatic: Inside lay floral carpets, rush mats, red brocaded cushions, and a cinnabar chair with gilded dragon.

sentences.zh: 靠背以下諸制與大小馬輦並同。

translations.literal: From the backrest downward all regulations were the same as the great and small horse palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: From the backrest down, all matched the great and small horse palanquins.

sentences.zh: 輦頂並圓盤高二尺六寸有奇，鍍金銅蹲龍頂，餘制同大小馬輦。

translations.literal: The palanquin top together with the round plate more than two chi six cun high; gilded copper crouching-dragon top; remaining regulations the same as the great and small horse palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy and plate together exceeded two chi six cun, with a gilded crouching dragon; all else matched the horse palanquins.

sentences.zh: 天輪制亦如之。

translations.literal: The heaven wheel regulations were also the same.
translations.idiomatic: The heaven wheel followed the same rules.

sentences.zh: 輦亭前左右轉角闌干二扇，後一字帶左右轉角闌干一扇，皆硃魨，嵌雕木貼金龍，間以五彩雲。

translations.literal: Before the palanquin pavilion left and right corner-turning railings two panels; behind one straight panel with left and right corner-turning railings—all cinnabar-lacquered, inlaid carved wood gilded dragons, interspersed with five-colored clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Corner rails fore and aft enclosed the pavilion in cinnabar, inlaid with gilded dragons and five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 三扇凡十有二柱，各柱首雕飾與大輅同。

translations.literal: The three panels totaled twelve pillars; each pillar-top ornament the same as the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pillars on three panels bore caps matching the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 闌內四周布花毯草席。

translations.literal: Within the rails floral carpets and rush mats spread all around.
translations.idiomatic: Floral carpets and rush mats lined the interior.

sentences.zh: 亭內木雕渾貼金劍山一，硃魨腳踏一，黃緞衣全。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion one carved wholly gilded sword-mountain of wood, one cinnabar-lacquered footrest, yellow satin garments complete.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood a gilded wooden sword-mountain, a cinnabar footrest, and yellow satin garments.

sentences.zh: 踏梯一，木質硃魨，雕貼金行龍五彩雲絛環板六片，描金五彩水板十有二片，蹲龍四，皆抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: One mounting ladder, wooden cinnabar-lacquered, carved gilded traveling-dragon five-colored cloud ring panels six pieces, gold-traced five-colored water panels twelve pieces, crouching dragons four—all gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: One cinnabar ladder bore six gilded dragon panels, twelve water panels, and four crouching dragons in gold.

sentences.zh: 其幰衣、雨衣類悉同大小馬輦制。

translations.literal: Canopy coat, raincoat, and the like all followed the great and small horse palanquin regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy coats and rain gear followed the horse palanquin rules.

sentences.zh: 革輅，服馬一，驂馬三，亦設游環和鈴，圓蓋方軫。

translations.literal: The leather chariot: one harness horse, three outrider horses, also with swinging rings and harmony bells; round canopy and square frame.
translations.idiomatic: The leather chariot used one harness horse and three outriders, with harmony bells, a round canopy, and square frame.

sentences.zh: 高一丈一尺三寸，蓋高二尺五寸五分，泥銀飾銜圓黃革四。

translations.literal: Height one zhang one chi three cun; canopy two chi five cun five fen high; clay-silver ornamentation holding four round yellow leather plaques.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one zhang, one chi, and three cun high; the canopy two chi, five cun, and five fen, in clay-silver trim with four round yellow leather plaques.

sentences.zh: 白緞垂幨三層，系帶四，亦白緞為之，屬於軫。

translations.literal: Three layers of white satin hanging curtains; four fastening bands, also of white satin, attached to the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Three tiers of white satin curtains hung below, with four white satin bands on the frame.

sentences.zh: 四柱高五尺五寸九分，座縱一丈六尺，橫八尺三寸五分，環以硃闌。

translations.literal: Four pillars five chi five cun nine fen high; seat one zhang six chi long, eight chi three cun five fen wide, encircled by vermilion rails.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each five chi, five cun, and nine fen tall, supported a platform one zhang six chi by eight chi, three cun, and five fen, ringed in vermilion rails.

sentences.zh: 轅二，各長一丈九尺五分，軫長一丈六寸，徑八尺三寸五分。

translations.literal: Two shafts, each one zhang nine chi five fen long; frame one zhang six cun long, diameter eight chi three cun five fen.
translations.idiomatic: Two shafts, each one zhang, nine chi, and five fen long, joined a frame one zhang six cun wide and eight chi, three cun, and five fen across.

sentences.zh: 後建大白，十有二斿，各綉金虎，餘制均與玉輅同。

translations.literal: Behind was erected the Great White, twelve pennants, each embroidered with a gold tiger; remaining regulations all the same as the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Behind rose the Great White banner with twelve pennants, each bearing a golden tiger; all else matched the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 按改小馬輦為革輅，始於乾隆八年。

translations.literal: As for changing the small horse palanquin to the leather chariot, it began in the eighth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: The leather chariot replaced the small horse palanquin beginning in Qianlong 8.

sentences.zh: 初制，小馬輦視大馬輦高廣皆減一尺。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the small horse palanquin in height and width was each one chi less than the great horse palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the small horse palanquin was one chi shorter and narrower than the great horse palanquin.

sentences.zh: 下二轅長一丈九尺五分。

translations.literal: The two lower shafts one zhang nine chi five fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Its two lower shafts were one zhang, nine chi, and five fen long.

sentences.zh: 平盤、滴珠板、輪輻、輪輞諸制悉?大馬輦同。

translations.literal: Flat plate, pearl-drip board, spokes, rims—all regulations the same as the great horse palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Platform, pearl-drip board, spokes, and rims all followed the great horse palanquin.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高五尺五寸九分，硃魨。

translations.literal: The palanquin pavilion five chi five cun nine fen high, cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion stood five chi, five cun, and nine fen high, in cinnabar lacquer.

sentences.zh: 四柱長五尺四寸五分。

translations.literal: The four pillars five chi four cun five fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each five chi, four cun, and five fen long.

sentences.zh: 檻高一寸四分，上四周雕沈香色描金雲板十二片，下亦如之。

translations.literal: The railing one cun four fen high; above on four sides twelve carved agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud panels; below likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The railing rose one cun and four fen, with twelve agarwood-toned cloud panels above and below.

sentences.zh: 門高五尺，廣二尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: The door five chi high, two chi two cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors measured five chi high by two chi, two cun, and five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 左右門廣較減一寸有奇。

translations.literal: The left and right doors were more than one cun narrower in width.
translations.idiomatic: Side doors were over one cun narrower.

sentences.zh: 前左右各有槅二扇，明栨全，皆硃魨，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Front left and right each had two lattice-panel leaves, bright panels complete, all cinnabar-lacquered, gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Fore and side doors were two cinnabar lattice panels each, studded with gilded floral plates.

sentences.zh: 槅心編黃線絛。

translations.literal: The lattice centers were woven with yellow cord tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Lattice centers were bound with yellow cord.

sentences.zh: 後硃魨屏風，雕沈香色描金雲龍五，及沈香色描金雲龍絛環板三，雲板數亦如之。

translations.literal: Behind, a cinnabar-lacquered screen; five carved agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragons, and three agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragon ring panels; cloud panels in corresponding number.
translations.idiomatic: Behind stood a cinnabar screen with five agarwood-toned dragons and three matching ring panels.

sentences.zh: 周圍亦抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: All around also gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded floral plates studded the surroundings as well.

sentences.zh: 亭座硃魨板上施素毯草席，紅織金綺褥。

translations.literal: On the pavilion seat cinnabar-lacquered boards were laid plain mats and rush mats, red brocaded gold cushions.
translations.idiomatic: The cinnabar seat bore plain mats, rush mats, and red brocaded gold cushions.

sentences.zh: 外紅簾四扇，其坐椅靠背以下諸制悉同大馬輦。

translations.literal: Outside, four red curtains; from the chair backrest downward all regulations were the same as the great horse palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Four red curtains hung outside; chair and fittings matched the great horse palanquin.

sentences.zh: 輦頂並圓盤高視大馬輦減一寸。

translations.literal: The palanquin top together with the round plate one cun lower than the great horse palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy and plate sat one cun lower than on the great horse palanquin.

sentences.zh: 上飾鍍金銅寶珠頂。

translations.literal: Above ornamented with a gilded copper treasured-pearl top.
translations.idiomatic: A gilded copper jeweled finial crowned the top.

sentences.zh: 蓮座、寶蓋等飾，及天輪、輦亭前諸制，亦與大馬輦同焉。

translations.literal: Lotus seat, treasured canopy, and other ornaments, and heaven wheel, palanquin pavilion front regulations, were also the same as the great horse palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Lotus seat, treasured canopy, heaven wheel, and pavilion fittings matched the great horse palanquin.

sentences.zh: 古玉輦，木質魨硃，圓蓋方座。

translations.literal: The ancient jade palanquin: wooden, cinnabar-lacquered, round canopy and square seat.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient jade palanquin was wooden, cinnabar-lacquered, with a round canopy on a square seat.

sentences.zh: 高一丈一尺一寸，蓋高二尺，青飾、銜玉圓版四。

translations.literal: Height one zhang one chi one cun; canopy two chi high; green ornamentation holding four jade round plaques.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one zhang, one chi, and one cun high; the canopy two chi, in green with four jade round plaques.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂，承以鏤金垂雲。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top, supported by openwork gilded hanging clouds.
translations.idiomatic: A gilded round cap bore openwork gilded cloud eaves.

sentences.zh: 曲梁四垂，端為金雲葉。

translations.literal: Curved beams draped on four sides; the ends were gold cloud leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Curved beams hung on four sides, their ends shaped as gilded cloud leaves.

sentences.zh: 青緞垂幨二層，周為襞積。

translations.literal: Two layers of green satin hanging curtains, pleated all around.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiers of green satin curtains hung in pleats around the sides.

sentences.zh: 系紃四，黃絨為之，屬於座隅。

translations.literal: Four fastening cords, of yellow velvet, attached to the seat corners.
translations.idiomatic: Four yellow velvet cords were tied to the seat corners.

sentences.zh: 四柱高五尺三寸，相距各五尺，繪雲龍。

translations.literal: Four pillars five chi three cun high, each spaced five chi apart, painted with cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each five chi and three cun tall and five chi apart, were painted with cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 門高四尺八寸，冬施青氈門幃，夏易以硃簾，黑緞緣，四面各三。

translations.literal: The door four chi eight cun high; in winter green felt door curtains were hung; in summer changed to vermilion curtains with black satin borders, three on each of four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Doors stood four chi eight cun high; winter brought green felt curtains, summer vermilion curtains with black satin borders, three per side.

sentences.zh: 座高二尺四寸，上方七尺六寸，下方七尺七寸，綴版二層，上繪彩雲，下繪金雲，環以硃闌，高一尺六寸八分，飾間金彩。

translations.literal: The seat two chi four cun high; above seven chi six cun, below seven chi seven cun; two layers of panels attached; above painted colored clouds, below painted gold clouds; encircled by vermilion rails one chi six cun eight fen high, ornamented with inset gold coloring.
translations.idiomatic: The seat rose two chi four cun on a platform seven chi six cun above and seven chi seven cun below, with colored clouds above and golden clouds below, ringed by vermilion rails one chi six cun eight fen high inlaid with gold.

sentences.zh: 闌內周布花毯。

translations.literal: Within the rails floral carpets spread all around.
translations.idiomatic: Floral carpets lined the interior within the rails.

sentences.zh: 雲龍寶座在中，高一尺三寸。

translations.literal: The cloud-dragon throne in the center, one chi three cun high.
translations.idiomatic: At the center stood the cloud-dragon throne, one chi and three cun high.

sentences.zh: 左列銅鼎，右植服劍。

translations.literal: On the left were arranged bronze tripods; on the right were planted ceremonial sword and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze tripods stood to the left; ceremonial sword and robes to the right.

sentences.zh: 轅四，內二轅長三丈八寸五分，外二轅長二丈九尺，金龍首尾銜兩端。

translations.literal: Four shafts; the inner two shafts three zhang eight cun five fen long, the outer two shafts two zhang nine chi long, with gold dragon heads and tails joining both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Four shafts: inner pair three zhang eight cun five fen, outer pair two zhang nine chi, capped with golden dragon heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 升用納陛五級，左右闌皆魨硃，亦飾金彩，舁以三十六人。

translations.literal: To ascend, five steps of recessed tread were used; left and right rails all cinnabar-lacquered, also ornamented with gold coloring; carried by thirty-six men.
translations.idiomatic: Five recessed steps led up between cinnabar rails trimmed in gold; thirty-six bearers carried it.

sentences.zh: 金輦，圓蓋方軫。

translations.literal: The gold palanquin: round canopy and square frame.
translations.idiomatic: The gold palanquin had a round canopy and square frame.

sentences.zh: 高一丈五尺，蓋高一尺九寸，飾蓋用泥金銜金圓版四。

translations.literal: Height one zhang five chi; canopy one chi nine cun high; canopy ornament used clay-gold holding four gold round plaques.
translations.idiomatic: It stood one zhang and five chi high; the canopy one chi nine cun, in clay-gold with four gold round plaques.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top.
translations.idiomatic: It was crowned with a gilded round cap.

sentences.zh: 檐徑七尺一寸。

translations.literal: The eaves diameter seven chi one cun.
translations.idiomatic: The eaves spanned seven chi and one cun.

sentences.zh: 黃緞垂幨二層。

translations.literal: Two layers of yellow satin hanging curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiers of yellow satin curtains hung below.

sentences.zh: 柱高五尺，相距各四尺九寸。

translations.literal: Pillars five chi high, each spaced four chi nine cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: Pillars five chi tall stood four chi nine cun apart.

sentences.zh: 門高四尺七寸五分。

translations.literal: The door four chi seven cun five fen high.
translations.idiomatic: Doors stood four chi, seven cun, and five fen high.

sentences.zh: 冬垂黃氈門幃，夏易以硃簾，黑緞緣，四面各三。

translations.literal: In winter yellow felt door curtains hung; in summer changed to vermilion curtains with black satin borders, three on each of four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought yellow felt door curtains; summer vermilion curtains with black satin borders, three per side.

sentences.zh: 座上方七尺三寸，下方七尺五寸，環以硃闌，高一尺三寸。

translations.literal: The seat above seven chi three cun, below seven chi five cun; encircled by vermilion rails one chi three cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The platform measured seven chi three cun above and seven chi five cun below, ringed by vermilion rails one chi three cun high.

sentences.zh: 轅四，內二轅長二丈八尺一寸，外二轅長二丈六尺一寸。

translations.literal: Four shafts; the inner two shafts two zhang eight chi one cun long, the outer two shafts two zhang six chi one cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Four shafts: inner pair two zhang eight chi one cun, outer pair two zhang six chi one cun.

sentences.zh: 舁以二十八人。

translations.literal: Carried by twenty-eight men.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight bearers carried it.

sentences.zh: 餘如玉輦之制。

translations.literal: The remainder like the jade palanquin regulations.
translations.idiomatic: All else followed the jade palanquin.

sentences.zh: 按乾隆十三年，改涼步輦為金輦。

translations.literal: As for the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the cool step palanquin was changed to the gold palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 the cool step palanquin became the gold palanquin.

sentences.zh: 初制，涼步輦高一丈一尺二寸，座高二尺五寸。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the cool step palanquin was one zhang one chi two cun high; the seat two chi five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the cool step palanquin stood one zhang, one chi, and two cun high, its seat two chi five cun high.

sentences.zh: 輦座硃魨，座板並四面硃魨匡，雕木渾貼金雲板二十片，上貼金地雕五彩雲絛環板十二片，帶仰覆蓮座。

translations.literal: The palanquin seat cinnabar-lacquered; seat boards and four-sided cinnabar-lacquered frames; twenty carved wood wholly gilded cloud panels; above twelve gold-ground carved five-colored cloud ring panels, with inverted lotus seats.
translations.idiomatic: Its cinnabar seat and frame bore twenty wholly gilded cloud panels and twelve five-colored ring panels on gold ground with lotus seats.

sentences.zh: 下四轅，中二轅長二丈八尺五寸，左右二轅長較減二尺，皆硃魨，前後俱鍍金銅龍首尾裝釘，攀轅黃線圓絛八。

translations.literal: Below four shafts; the middle two shafts two zhang eight chi five cun long, the left and right two shafts two chi shorter, all cinnabar-lacquered; front and rear both gilded copper dragon heads and tails nailed on; eight yellow cord round tassels for pulling the shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Four shafts below: center pair two zhang eight chi five cun, side pair two chi shorter—all cinnabar, with gilded dragon caps and eight yellow pulling cords.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高五尺五寸五分，方四尺八寸，硃魨。

translations.literal: The palanquin pavilion five chi five cun five fen high, square four chi eight cun, cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion stood five chi, five cun, and five fen high on a four chi eight cun square base, in cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 門高四尺七寸，廣二尺二寸。

translations.literal: The door four chi seven cun high, two chi two cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors measured four chi seven cun high by two chi two cun wide.

sentences.zh: 左右門廣亦如之。

translations.literal: The left and right doors were likewise in width.
translations.idiomatic: Side doors were equally wide.

sentences.zh: 上四周沈香色描金香草板十二片，前左右各有槅二扇，後槅三扇，明栨全，皆硃魨，編以黃線絛。

translations.literal: Above on four sides twelve agarwood-colored gold-traced vanilla panels; front left and right each two lattice-panel leaves; rear three lattice-panel leaves; bright panels complete, all cinnabar-lacquered, woven with yellow cord tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve agarwood-toned floral panels crowned the frame; fore and side doors were two cinnabar lattice panels each, the rear three, all bound with yellow cord.

sentences.zh: 輦板上施花毯草席，並紅織金綺褥。

translations.literal: On the palanquin boards floral carpets and rush mats were laid, together with red brocaded gold cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Floral carpets, rush mats, and red brocaded cushions covered the floor.

sentences.zh: 硃魨戧金雲龍坐椅一，坐下四周雕木沈香色描金雲，其上靠背雕沈香色描金龍一，並五彩雲，下雕貼金雲板一片，硃魨福壽板一，並衣。

translations.literal: One cinnabar-lacquered gilded cloud-dragon chair; below on four sides carved wood agarwood-colored gold-traced clouds; above the backrest one carved agarwood-colored gold-traced dragon, and five-colored clouds; below one applied gilded cloud panel; one cinnabar fortune-longevity panel; garments complete.
translations.idiomatic: A cinnabar chair with gilded cloud-dragons bore one agarwood-toned dragon on its back, a gilded cloud panel below, and a fortune-longevity panel with garments complete.

sentences.zh: 亭內設雕木渾貼金劍山一，腳踏一，黃緞衣全。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion one carved wholly gilded sword-mountain of wood was set, one footrest, yellow satin garments complete.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood a gilded sword-mountain, a footrest, and yellow satin garments.

sentences.zh: 銅火爐及鍍金鑲嵌寶石銅爐各一，坐褥、椅裙、簾幔之類，悉與大小馬輦同。

translations.literal: One copper brazier and one gilded inset precious-stone copper brazier each; seat cushions, chair skirts, curtain drapes, and the like—all the same as the great and small horse palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Copper and gilded gem-set braziers, cushions, skirts, and drapes matched the horse palanquins.

sentences.zh: 輦頂高二尺五寸，鍍金銅寶珠頂，帶仰覆蓮座，高一尺三寸二分，垂攀頂黃絨索四。

translations.literal: The palanquin top two chi five cun high; gilded copper treasured-pearl top, with inverted lotus seat one chi three cun two fen high; four yellow velvet cords hung from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy rose two chi five cun, crowned by a gilded jeweled finial on a lotus base one chi three cun two fen high, with four yellow climbing cords.

sentences.zh: 頂硃魨，冒以黃氈，四角如意雲並緣絛，亦均黃氈為之。

translations.literal: The top cinnabar-lacquered, covered with yellow felt; four corners ruyi clouds and border tassels, also all of yellow felt.
translations.idiomatic: The cinnabar top was veiled in yellow felt, with ruyi clouds and felt border tassels at the corners.

sentences.zh: 周圍施金黃綺瀝水二層，每層百二十四摺，綉雲龍，間以五彩雲文。

translations.literal: All around were two layers of golden-yellow brocade eaves-drip, each layer one hundred twenty-four folds, embroidered cloud-dragons, interspersed with five-colored cloud patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiers of golden brocade eaves, one hundred twenty-four folds each, bore embroidered cloud-dragons and five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 腰綉行龍十六。

translations.literal: The waist embroidered sixteen traveling dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The waistband bore sixteen traveling dragons in embroidery.

sentences.zh: 或大紅羅冒頂，如意雲緣絛亦紅羅為之。

translations.literal: Or a great red gauze canopy top; ruyi cloud border tassels also of red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively a great red gauze canopy with red gauze ruyi borders.

sentences.zh: 四角鍍金銅雲四朵。

translations.literal: At the four corners four gilded copper clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Four gilded copper cloud ornaments stood at the corners.

sentences.zh: 亭內寶蓋綉五龍，頂用硃魨木匡，冒以黃綺，謂之黃屋。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion the treasured canopy embroidered five dragons; the top used a cinnabar-lacquered wood frame, covered with yellow brocade—called the Yellow Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, a treasured canopy on a cinnabar frame veiled in yellow brocade—the Yellow Canopy—bore five embroidered dragons.

sentences.zh: 頂心四周綉雲龍各一。

translations.literal: Around the top center four sides embroidered one cloud-dragon each.
translations.idiomatic: Four cloud-dragons were embroidered around the apex.

sentences.zh: 輦亭四角至輦座攀頂黃線圓絛四，並貼金木魚。

translations.literal: From the four corners of the palanquin pavilion to the palanquin seat, four yellow cord round tassels for the climbing top, and gilded wood fish.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow climbing cords and gilded wooden fish linked pavilion corners to the seat.

sentences.zh: 亭外圍紅氈面、金黃氈緣絛、絹里氈衣一副。

translations.literal: Outside the pavilion one set of red felt-faced, golden-yellow felt-bordered, silk-lined felt garments.
translations.idiomatic: Outside hung a red felt garment with golden-yellow felt borders and silk lining.

sentences.zh: 輦亭前左右轉角闌干二扇，後一字帶轉角闌干二扇，皆硃魨，雕木玲瓏金地五彩妝雲板十六片。
