translations.literal: Before the palanquin pavilion left and right corner-turning railings two panels; behind one straight panel with corner-turning railings two panels—all cinnabar-lacquered; sixteen carved wood openwork gold-ground five-colored cloud panels.
translations.idiomatic: Corner rails enclosed the pavilion in cinnabar, set with sixteen openwork gilded five-colored cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 四扇凡十二柱，各柱首雕飾同大輅。

translations.literal: The four panels totaled twelve pillars; each pillar-top ornament the same as the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pillars on four panels bore caps matching the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 闌內四周施花毯草席，踏梯一，木質硃魨，貼金五彩雲玲瓏板六片，描金水板十二片。

translations.literal: Within the rails floral carpets and rush mats spread all around; one mounting ladder, wooden cinnabar-lacquered, six applied gold five-colored cloud openwork panels, twelve gold-traced water panels.
translations.idiomatic: Floral carpets and rush mats lined the interior; one cinnabar ladder bore six gilded cloud panels and twelve water panels.

sentences.zh: 蹲龍四，皆抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Four crouching dragons, all gilded copper inlaid floral leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: Four crouching dragons, all studded with gilded floral plates.

sentences.zh: 又鍍金銅鉤四，金黃線圓絛，數亦如之。

translations.literal: Moreover four gilded copper hooks, golden-yellow cord round tassels, equal in number.
translations.idiomatic: Four gilded hooks and matching golden-yellow cords completed the set.

sentences.zh: 紅油高凳四，黃氈輓凳二，金黃布夾幰衣、金黃油綢雨衣各一。

translations.literal: Four red-oiled high stools; two yellow felt carrying stools; one each of golden-yellow cloth-lined canopy coat and golden-yellow oiled-silk raincoat.
translations.idiomatic: It carried four red-oiled stools, two yellow felt stools, a golden-yellow canopy coat, and a golden-yellow raincoat.

sentences.zh: 禮輿，棻質。

translations.literal: The ritual litter: fragrant wood.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual litter was of fragrant wood.

sentences.zh: 高六尺三寸。

translations.literal: Height six chi three cun.
translations.idiomatic: It stood six chi and three cun high.

sentences.zh: 上為穹蓋二層，高一尺三寸。

translations.literal: Above was a domed canopy in two layers, one chi three cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Above rose a two-tier domed canopy one chi three cun high.

sentences.zh: 上層八角，飾金行龍。

translations.literal: The upper layer octagonal, ornamented with gilded traveling dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier was octagonal, trimmed with gilded traveling dragons.

sentences.zh: 下四角，飾亦如之。

translations.literal: The lower four corners, ornamentation likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The lower four corners were ornamented likewise.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂，承以鏤金垂雲，雜寶銜之。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top, supported by openwork gilded hanging clouds, miscellaneous treasures holding it.
translations.idiomatic: A gilded round cap bore openwork cloud eaves hung with miscellaneous treasure motifs.

sentences.zh: 檐縱四尺七寸，橫三尺五寸。

translations.literal: The eaves eight chi seven cun long, three chi five cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: The eaves measured eight chi seven cun by three chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 明黃緞垂幨二層，綉金雲龍。

translations.literal: Two layers of bright yellow satin hanging curtains, embroidered with gold cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiers of bright yellow satin curtains bore gold cloud-dragons in embroidery.

sentences.zh: 四柱高五尺，飾蟠龍，門端及左右闌飾雲龍，皆鏤金。

translations.literal: Four pillars five chi high, ornamented with coiled dragons; door ends and left and right rails ornamented with cloud-dragons—all openwork gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars five chi tall bore coiled dragons in openwork gold; doors and rails showed cloud-dragons likewise.

sentences.zh: 內設金龍寶座，高一尺七寸，幃用明黃雲緞紗氈，各惟其時。

translations.literal: Within was set a gold dragon throne, one chi seven cun high; curtains used bright yellow cloud satin, gauze, and felt, each according to the season.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood a golden dragon throne one chi seven cun high, with bright yellow cloud satin, gauze, or felt curtains by season.

sentences.zh: 左右啟櫺，夏用藍紗，冬用玻璃。

translations.literal: Left and right opened lattice windows; in summer blue gauze, in winter glass.
translations.idiomatic: Lattice windows on either side used blue gauze in summer and glass in winter.

sentences.zh: 直轅二，長一丈七尺六寸五分。

translations.literal: Two straight shafts, one zhang seven chi six cun five fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Two straight shafts, each one zhang, seven chi, six cun, and five fen long.

sentences.zh: 大橫杆二，長九尺。

translations.literal: Two great crossbars, nine chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Two great crossbars, nine chi long.

sentences.zh: 小橫杆四，長二尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: Four small crossbars, two chi two cun five fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Four small crossbars, two chi, two cun, and five fen long.

sentences.zh: 肩桿八，長五尺八寸。

translations.literal: Eight shoulder poles, five chi eight cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Eight shoulder poles, each five chi eight cun long.

sentences.zh: 皆魨硃，繪金雲龍。

translations.literal: All cinnabar-lacquered, painted with gold cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: All were cinnabar-lacquered and painted with golden cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 橫鑽銅，縱加金龍首尾。

translations.literal: Transversely drilled with copper; longitudinally added gold dragon heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: Copper pins crossed them lengthwise, capped with golden dragon heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 舁以十六人。

translations.literal: Carried by sixteen men.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen bearers carried it.

sentences.zh: 按禮輿為大儀轎之改定。

translations.literal: As for the ritual litter, it was reformed from the great ceremonial sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual litter was redesignated from the great ceremonial sedan.

sentences.zh: 初制，大儀轎高四尺八寸五分，頂高一尺三寸，廣二尺八寸。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the great ceremonial sedan was four chi eight cun five fen high; the top one chi three cun high, two chi eight cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the great ceremonial sedan stood four chi, eight cun, and five fen high, its canopy one chi three cun high and two chi eight cun wide.

sentences.zh: 頂雙層，渾貼金雕九龍，雲花番草絛環，銷金龍瀝水二層，黃綾為之。

translations.literal: The top in two layers, wholly gilded carved nine dragons; cloud, flower, and scroll ring panels; two layers of gilded dragon eaves-drip, of yellow gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Its two-tier canopy bore nine wholly gilded dragons, scroll ring panels, and two tiers of yellow gauze dragon eaves.

sentences.zh: 魨金直竿二，前後橫竿如之。

translations.literal: Two cinnabar-gilded straight poles; front and rear cross poles likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Two cinnabar-gilded straight poles and matching fore-and-aft crossbars.

sentences.zh: 短扛四，肩扛倍之。

translations.literal: Four short carrying poles; shoulder poles twice that number.
translations.idiomatic: Four short poles and twice as many shoulder poles.

sentences.zh: 撐竿二。

translations.literal: Two support poles.
translations.idiomatic: Two support poles.

sentences.zh: 轎頂蹲龍十二，金頂鈒龍文，嵌珊瑚青金松子等石。

translations.literal: On the sedan top twelve crouching dragons; the gold top inlaid with dragon patterns, inset coral, blue gold, pine-seed, and other stones.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve crouching dragons crowned the canopy; the gilded top was inlaid with dragon motifs, coral, lapis, and other stones.

sentences.zh: 轎扛裝鍍金銅龍首尾。

translations.literal: The sedan carrying poles fitted with gilded copper dragon heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying poles were capped with gilded copper dragon heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 黃布幰衣、油綢雨衣、黃氈頂各一。

translations.literal: One each of yellow cloth canopy coat, oiled-silk raincoat, and yellow felt top.
translations.idiomatic: It carried a yellow canopy coat, oiled-silk raincoat, and yellow felt top.

sentences.zh: 輕步輿，亦舁以十六人，木質魨硃，不施幰。

translations.literal: The light step litter, also carried by sixteen men; wooden, cinnabar-lacquered, without canopy curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The light step litter, borne by sixteen men, was wooden and cinnabar-lacquered, without canopy curtains.

sentences.zh: 蓋高三尺四寸。

translations.literal: The canopy three chi four cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy rose three chi and four cun.

sentences.zh: 倚高一尺五寸八分，象牙為之。

translations.literal: The armrest one chi five cun eight fen high, of ivory.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory armrests stood one chi, five cun, and eight fen high.

sentences.zh: 座高一尺八寸二分，縱一尺八寸三分，橫二尺二寸。

translations.literal: The seat one chi eight cun two fen high, one chi eight cun three fen long, two chi two cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: The seat rose one chi eight cun two fen on a platform one chi eight cun three fen by two chi two cun.

sentences.zh: 踏幾高三寸，魨以金。

translations.literal: The footrest three cun high, lacquered with gold.
translations.idiomatic: A three-cun footrest was gold-lacquered.

sentences.zh: 直轅二，長一丈五尺四寸五分，加銅龍首尾。

translations.literal: Two straight shafts, one zhang five chi four cun five fen long, with copper dragon heads and tails added.
translations.idiomatic: Two straight shafts, each one zhang five chi four cun five fen, bore copper dragon caps.

sentences.zh: 大橫杆二，長九尺一寸。

translations.literal: Two great crossbars, nine chi one cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Two great crossbars, nine chi one cun long.

sentences.zh: 小橫杆四，長二尺八寸四分。

translations.literal: Four small crossbars, two chi eight cun four fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Four small crossbars, two chi eight cun four fen long.

sentences.zh: 肩桿八，長五尺八寸五分，俱鑽銅。

translations.literal: Eight shoulder poles, five chi eight cun five fen long, all drilled with copper.
translations.idiomatic: Eight shoulder poles, each five chi eight cun five fen, were copper-drilled.

sentences.zh: 餘制與步輿同。

translations.literal: The remaining regulations the same as the step litter.
translations.idiomatic: All else followed the step litter.

sentences.zh: 按輕步輿之稱，改由折合明轎。

translations.literal: As for the light step litter name, it was changed from the folding bright sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The light step litter was redesignated from the folding bright sedan.

sentences.zh: 初制，折合明轎，金漆雕花草獸面。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the folding bright sedan: gold lacquer carved with flowers, grasses, and beast faces.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the folding bright sedan was gold-lacquered with floral and beast-face carving.

sentences.zh: 廣二尺二寸，高三尺四寸。

translations.literal: Two chi two cun wide, three chi four cun high.
translations.idiomatic: It measured two chi two cun wide and three chi four cun high.

sentences.zh: 地平廣如轎身。

translations.literal: The ground level as wide as the sedan body.
translations.idiomatic: Its floor matched the sedan body in width.

sentences.zh: 直竿下數亦如大儀轎。

translations.literal: The number of straight poles below was also like the great ceremonial sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Its straight poles below matched the great ceremonial sedan in number.

sentences.zh: 裝飾、幰衣諸制並與明轎同。

translations.literal: Ornament, canopy coat, and other regulations were all the same as the bright sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Ornament and canopy gear matched the bright sedan.

sentences.zh: 步輿，亦舁以十六人，木質塗金，不施幰。

translations.literal: The step litter, also carried by sixteen men; wooden with gold paint, without canopy curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The step litter, borne by sixteen men, was wood painted gold, without canopy curtains.

sentences.zh: 蓋高三尺五寸。

translations.literal: The canopy three chi five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy rose three chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 倚高一尺六寸五分，鏤花文。

translations.literal: The armrest one chi six cun five fen high, with openwork floral patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Openwork floral armrests stood one chi six cun five fen high.

sentences.zh: 中為蟠龍座，座高一尺八寸五分，縱一尺八寸，橫二尺二寸。

translations.literal: In the center was a coiled-dragon seat; the seat one chi eight cun five fen high, one chi eight cun long, two chi two cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: A coiled-dragon seat rose one chi eight cun five fen on a platform one chi eight cun by two chi two cun.

sentences.zh: 坐具冬施紫貂，夏以明黃妝緞。

translations.literal: Seat furnishings: in winter purple sable, in summer bright yellow brocaded satin.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought purple sable cushions; summer bright yellow brocaded satin.

sentences.zh: 四足為虎爪螭首，圓珠承之，周繪雲龍。

translations.literal: The four legs were tiger claws with chi-dragon heads, round pearls supporting them; cloud-dragons painted all around.
translations.idiomatic: Four legs shaped as tiger claws with chi-dragon heads on round pearl feet bore painted cloud-dragons around.

sentences.zh: 踏幾高三寸一分，籠以黃緞。

translations.literal: The footrest three cun one fen high, covered with yellow satin.
translations.idiomatic: A footrest three cun one fen high was covered in yellow satin.

sentences.zh: 直轅二，長一丈五尺五寸。

translations.literal: Two straight shafts, one zhang five chi five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Two straight shafts, each one zhang five chi five cun long.

sentences.zh: 大橫杆二，長七尺六寸，中為雙龍首相對。

translations.literal: Two great crossbars, seven chi six cun long; in the center two dragon heads facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Two great crossbars seven chi six cun long bore confronting dragon heads at center.

sentences.zh: 小橫杆四，長二尺八寸。

translations.literal: Four small crossbars, two chi eight cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Four small crossbars, two chi eight cun long.

sentences.zh: 肩桿八，長五尺六寸。

translations.literal: Eight shoulder poles, five chi six cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Eight shoulder poles, each five chi six cun long.

sentences.zh: 餘同禮輿之制。

translations.literal: The remainder the same as the ritual litter regulations.
translations.idiomatic: All else followed the ritual litter.

sentences.zh: 按步輿為大轎之改稱。

translations.literal: As for the step litter name, it was changed from the great sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The step litter was redesignated from the great sedan.

sentences.zh: 初制，大轎單頂硃魨，廣三尺，高五尺，貼金。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the great sedan: single top cinnabar-lacquered, three chi wide, five chi high, with applied gold.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the great sedan had a cinnabar single top three chi wide and five chi high with applied gold.

sentences.zh: 頂廣視轎身較贏八寸，高八寸。

translations.literal: The top width compared with the sedan body was eight cun wider; height eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: The top was eight cun wider and eight cun higher than the body.

sentences.zh: 銷金龍瀝水一層，黃綾為之。

translations.literal: One layer of gilded phoenix eaves-drip, of yellow gauze.
translations.idiomatic: One tier of yellow gauze phoenix eaves-drip was gilded.

sentences.zh: 飾金蹲龍四。

translations.literal: Four ornamented gold crouching phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Four gilded crouching phoenixes adorned it.

sentences.zh: 直竿下數亦如大儀轎。

translations.literal: The number of straight poles below was also like the great ceremonial sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Straight poles below matched the great ceremonial sedan in number.

sentences.zh: 金頂以下諸制並同。

translations.literal: From the gold top downward all regulations were the same.
translations.idiomatic: From the gilded top down, all matched.

sentences.zh: 皇后鳳輿，木質，魨明黃，高七尺。

translations.literal: The Empress phoenix litter: wooden, lacquered bright yellow, seven chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The empress phoenix litter was wood lacquered bright yellow, seven chi high.

sentences.zh: 穹蓋二重，高一尺五寸五分。

translations.literal: Domed canopy in two layers, one chi five cun five fen high.
translations.idiomatic: A two-tier domed canopy rose one chi five cun five fen.

sentences.zh: 上為八角，下方四隅，俱飾金鳳。

translations.literal: Above octagonal; below the four corners—all ornamented with gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier was octagonal; the lower four corners bore gilded phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂，鏤以雲文，雜寶銜之。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top, openwork with cloud patterns, miscellaneous treasures holding it.
translations.idiomatic: A gilded round cap bore openwork clouds and treasure motifs.

sentences.zh: 檐縱五尺，橫三尺七寸六分，明黃緞垂幨，上下皆銷金鳳。

translations.literal: The eaves five chi long, three chi seven cun six fen wide; bright yellow satin hanging curtains; above and below all with gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Eaves five chi by three chi seven cun six fen bore bright yellow curtains gilded with phoenixes above and below.

sentences.zh: 四柱，高四尺七寸，皆繪金鳳。

translations.literal: Four pillars, four chi seven cun high, all painted with gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each four chi seven cun tall, were painted with gilded phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 櫺四啟，網以青紃。

translations.literal: Four lattice windows opened; netted with green cord.
translations.idiomatic: Four lattice windows opened, screened with green cord.

sentences.zh: 前為雙扉，高二尺六寸，啟扉則舉櫺懸之，內魨淺紅。

translations.literal: In front double doors, two chi six cun high; when the doors opened the lattice was raised and hung; inside lacquered pale red.
translations.idiomatic: Double doors two chi six cun high opened to raised lattice screens; the interior was pale red lacquer.

sentences.zh: 中設硃座，高一尺七寸。

translations.literal: In the center was set a vermilion seat, one chi seven cun high.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion seat one chi seven cun high stood at center.

sentences.zh: 倚高一尺八寸，魨明黃，繪金鳳。

translations.literal: The armrest one chi eight cun high, lacquered bright yellow, painted with gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow armrests one chi eight cun high bore gilded phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 坐具明黃緞綉彩鳳。

translations.literal: Seat furnishings: bright yellow satin embroidered with colored phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow satin cushions were embroidered with colored phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 前加撫式，明黃金鳳魨繪亦如之。

translations.literal: In front was added an armrest-style extension; bright yellow gilded phoenix lacquer and painting likewise.
translations.idiomatic: A forward armrest extension matched the bright yellow gilded phoenix finish.

sentences.zh: 直轅二，長一丈七尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: Two straight shafts, one zhang seven chi two cun five fen long.
translations.idiomatic: Two straight shafts, each one zhang seven chi two cun five fen long.

sentences.zh: 大橫杆二，長八尺，中為鐵鋄金雙鳳相向。

translations.literal: Two great crossbars, eight chi long; in the center iron-clad gold double phoenixes facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Two eight-chi crossbars bore iron-clad golden confronting phoenixes at center.

sentences.zh: 小橫杆四，長三尺。

translations.literal: Four small crossbars, three chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Four small crossbars, three chi long.

sentences.zh: 肩桿八，長五尺一寸。

translations.literal: Eight shoulder poles, five chi one cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Eight shoulder poles, each five chi one cun long.

sentences.zh: 皆魨明黃，橫鑽以銅，縱加銅鋄金鳳首尾。

translations.literal: All lacquered bright yellow; transversely drilled with copper; longitudinally added copper-clad gold phoenix heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: All were bright yellow lacquer, copper-drilled, with copper-clad golden phoenix caps lengthwise.

sentences.zh: 舁以十六人。

translations.literal: Carried by sixteen men.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen bearers carried it.

sentences.zh: 親蠶御之。

translations.literal: Used by the empress when she personally tended the silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The empress rode it for the personal silkworm ceremony.

sentences.zh: 按后妃輿車之制，改定於乾隆十四年。

translations.literal: As for empress and consort carriage regulations, they were fixed in the fourteenth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages for empresses and consorts were codified in Qianlong 14.

sentences.zh: 初制，鳳輿外並有鳳輦，柱高三尺六寸，廣五尺二寸。

translations.literal: In the initial system, besides the phoenix litter there was also the phoenix palanquin; pillars three chi six cun high, five chi two cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Originally there was also a phoenix palanquin: pillars three chi six cun high, five chi two cun wide.

sentences.zh: 座高一尺八寸，周圍闌柱、絛環雕花卉，硃魨貼金飾。

translations.literal: The seat one chi eight cun high; surrounding rails and pillars, ring panels carved with flowers; cinnabar-lacquered applied gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Its seat rose one chi eight cun, ringed by floral rails and pillars in cinnabar and applied gold.

sentences.zh: 寶座在中，下有仙橋，座穿以藤。

translations.literal: The treasured seat in the center; below was an immortal bridge; the seat pierced with rattan.
translations.idiomatic: A treasured seat above an immortal bridge was pierced with rattan.

sentences.zh: 窗槅編石青線，頂衣用黃結羅為之。

translations.literal: Window lattice woven with stone-blue cord; the top garment used yellow knotted gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Windows were bound in stone-blue cord; the canopy cover was yellow knotted gauze.

sentences.zh: 銷金鳳瀝水二層。

translations.literal: Two layers of gilded phoenix eaves-drip.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiers of gilded phoenix eaves-drip.

sentences.zh: 黃緞裡衣。

translations.literal: Yellow satin lining garments.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow satin linings.

sentences.zh: 外垂珠簾。

translations.literal: Outside hung pearl curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Pearl curtains hung outside.

sentences.zh: 直竿四，內扛倍之。

translations.literal: Four straight poles; inner carrying poles twice that number.
translations.idiomatic: Four straight poles and twice as many inner carrying poles.

sentences.zh: 短扛如內扛之數。

translations.literal: Short carrying poles equal in number to the inner poles.
translations.idiomatic: Short poles matched the inner poles in number.

sentences.zh: 俱硃魨。

translations.literal: All cinnabar-lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: All were cinnabar-lacquered.

sentences.zh: 赤金頂鈒鳳文，嵌青金、珊瑚、松子等石。

translations.literal: The red-gold top inlaid with phoenix patterns, inset blue gold, coral, pine-seed, and other stones.
translations.idiomatic: The red-gold top was inlaid with phoenix motifs, lapis, coral, and other stones.

sentences.zh: 扛端裝金鳳首尾。

translations.literal: The pole ends fitted with gold phoenix heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: Pole ends bore golden phoenix heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 紅油凳四。

translations.literal: Four red-oiled stools.
translations.idiomatic: Four red-oiled stools.

sentences.zh: 拓叉二。

translations.literal: Two support forks.
translations.idiomatic: Two support forks.

sentences.zh: 黃布幰衣、油綢雨衣各一。

translations.literal: One each of yellow cloth canopy coat and oiled-silk raincoat.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow canopy coat and oiled-silk raincoat.

sentences.zh: 鳳輿制廣三尺一寸五分，柱高三尺三寸二分，門高二尺八寸，頂廣視面較贏八寸。

translations.literal: The phoenix litter regulations: three chi one cun five fen wide; pillars three chi three cun two fen high; door two chi eight cun high; the top width compared with the face was eight cun wider.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix litter was three chi one cun five fen wide, with pillars three chi three cun two fen, doors two chi eight cun, and a top eight cun wider than the face.

sentences.zh: 頂樓六瓣，每瓣廣一尺五寸，共高一尺二寸。

translations.literal: The top pavilion six petals; each petal one chi five cun wide, together one chi two cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy had six petals, each one chi five cun wide, together one chi two cun high.

sentences.zh: 轅長一丈七尺五寸，輪高五尺，俱施黃油彩繪金鳳。

translations.literal: The shafts one zhang seven chi five cun long; wheels five chi high—all with yellow oil and painted gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Shafts one zhang seven chi five cun and wheels five chi high were yellow-oiled and painted with gilded phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 赤金頂，鍍金葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Red-gold top, gilded leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: A red-gold top was studded with gilded plates.

sentences.zh: 黃素綾衣，上銷金鳳瀝水二層。

translations.literal: Plain yellow gauze garments; above two layers of gilded phoenix eaves-drip.
translations.idiomatic: Plain yellow gauze garments bore two tiers of gilded phoenix eaves.

sentences.zh: 儀輿，木質，魨以明黃，高視鳳輿減一尺一寸。

translations.literal: The ceremonial litter: wooden, lacquered bright yellow, one chi one cun lower than the phoenix litter.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial litter was wood lacquered bright yellow, one chi one cun shorter than the phoenix litter.

sentences.zh: 上為穹蓋，高六寸七分。

translations.literal: Above was a domed canopy, six cun seven fen high.
translations.idiomatic: A domed canopy rose six cun seven fen.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂，塗金檐，縱四尺七寸。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top, gilded eaves, five chi seven cun long.
translations.idiomatic: A gilded round cap and gilded eaves spanned five chi seven cun.

sentences.zh: 四隅系黃絨紃，屬於直轅。

translations.literal: At the four corners yellow velvet cords were attached, belonging to the straight shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow velvet cords at the four corners tied to the straight shafts.

sentences.zh: 明黃緞垂幨。

translations.literal: Bright yellow satin hanging curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow satin curtains hung below.

sentences.zh: 四柱，高四尺七寸。

translations.literal: Four pillars, four chi seven cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars, each four chi seven cun tall.

sentences.zh: 門幃紅里，亦明黃緞為之。

translations.literal: Door curtains red-lined, also of bright yellow satin.
translations.idiomatic: Door curtains were bright yellow satin with red lining.

sentences.zh: 中設硃座，高一尺五寸，倚魨明黃，高一尺六寸，繪金鳳。

translations.literal: In the center was set a vermilion seat, one chi five cun high; the armrest lacquered bright yellow, one chi six cun high, painted with gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion seat one chi five cun high had bright yellow armrests one chi six cun high painted with gilded phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 坐具明黃緞，綉彩鳳。

translations.literal: Seat furnishings bright yellow satin, embroidered with colored phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow satin cushions bore colored phoenixes in embroidery.

sentences.zh: 直轅二，長一丈五尺五寸。

translations.literal: Two straight shafts, one zhang five chi five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Two straight shafts, each one zhang five chi five cun long.

sentences.zh: 橫杆二，長七尺七寸，中為鐵鋄金雙鳳相向。

translations.literal: Two crossbars, seven chi seven cun long; in the center iron-clad gold double phoenixes facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Two crossbars seven chi seven cun long bore iron-clad golden confronting phoenixes at center.

sentences.zh: 肩桿四，長五尺二寸，兩端鑽銅鋄金。

translations.literal: Four shoulder poles, five chi two cun long; both ends drilled with copper-clad gold.
translations.idiomatic: Four shoulder poles five chi two cun long were copper-clad gold at both ends.

sentences.zh: 舁以八人。

translations.literal: Carried by eight men.
translations.idiomatic: Eight bearers carried it.

sentences.zh: 初制，儀輿廣三尺二寸，柱高三尺四寸，頂廣視面轅較贏三寸，高九寸，轅長與鳳輿同，輪較低二寸，俱施黃油。

translations.literal: In the initial system, the ceremonial litter was three chi two cun wide; pillars three chi four cun high; the top width compared with the face and shafts was three cun wider; height nine cun; shaft length the same as the phoenix litter; wheels two cun lower—all with yellow oil.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the ceremonial litter was three chi two cun wide, pillars three chi four cun, top three cun wider and nine cun higher than the face, shafts as long as the phoenix litter, wheels two cun lower—all yellow-oiled.

sentences.zh: 赤金頂，鍍金葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Red-gold top, gilded leaf pieces nailed on.
translations.idiomatic: A red-gold top was studded with gilded plates.

sentences.zh: 衣以黃雲緞為之。

translations.literal: Garments of yellow cloud satin.
translations.idiomatic: Garments were yellow cloud satin.

sentences.zh: 重檐瀝水，紅緞里。

translations.literal: Double-eaves drip, red satin lining.
translations.idiomatic: Double eaves with red satin lining.

sentences.zh: 黃布幰衣、油綢雨衣、黃氈頂各一。

translations.literal: One each of yellow cloth canopy coat, oiled-silk raincoat, and yellow felt top.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow canopy coat, oiled-silk raincoat, and yellow felt top.

sentences.zh: 鳳車，木質，檗明黃，高九尺五寸。

translations.literal: The phoenix carriage: wooden, lacquered bright yellow, nine chi five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix carriage was wood lacquered bright yellow, nine chi five cun high.

sentences.zh: 穹蓋二層，高一尺七寸，上繪八寶，八角飾以金鳳，下繪雲文，四隅飾亦如之。

translations.literal: Domed canopy two layers, one chi seven cun high; above painted the Eight Treasures; the octagon ornamented with gilded phoenixes; below painted cloud patterns; the four corners ornamented likewise.
translations.idiomatic: A two-tier dome one chi seven cun high bore the Eight Treasures above, gilded phoenixes on the octagon, clouds below, and matching corner ornaments.

sentences.zh: 冠金圓頂，鏤雲，雜寶銜之。

translations.literal: Crowned with a gilded round top, openwork clouds, miscellaneous treasures holding it.
translations.idiomatic: A gilded round cap bore openwork clouds and treasure motifs.

sentences.zh: 檐縱四尺九寸，橫四尺。

translations.literal: The eaves four chi nine cun long, four chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: Eaves measured four chi nine cun by four chi.

sentences.zh: 明黃緞垂幨，蓋明黃絡，四隅系紃，明黃絨為之，屬於軫。

translations.literal: Bright yellow satin hanging curtains; the canopy bright yellow net; at four corners cords attached, of bright yellow velvet, belonging to the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow satin curtains hung from a bright yellow net canopy; bright yellow velvet cords at the four corners tied to the frame.

sentences.zh: 四柱，高三尺三寸，左右及後皆繪金鳳。

translations.literal: Four pillars, three chi three cun high; left, right, and rear all painted with gilded phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars stood three chi three cun high; gilded phoenixes were painted on the left, right, and rear.

sentences.zh: 中各啟櫺，網以青紃，門高三尺，上鏤金鳳相向。

translations.literal: Each opened lattices in the middle, netted with blue cords; the door three chi high, above openwork gilded phoenixes facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Each side had latticed panels screened with blue cord; the door was three chi high, topped with facing gilded phoenixes in openwork.

sentences.zh: 明黃緞幃，黃里。

translations.literal: Bright yellow satin curtains, yellow lining.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow satin curtains with yellow lining.

sentences.zh: 坐具亦明黃緞為之，上綉彩鳳。

translations.literal: The seat cushion also of bright yellow satin, embroidered with colored phoenixes above.
translations.idiomatic: The seat cushion was also bright yellow satin, embroidered with colored phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 輪徑四尺九寸，各十有八輻。

translations.literal: Wheel diameter four chi nine cun; each had eighteen spokes.
translations.idiomatic: Wheels measured four chi nine cun in diameter, each with eighteen spokes.

sentences.zh: 轅二，長一丈七尺五寸，兩端鑽以鐵鋄金。

translations.literal: Two shafts, one zhang seven chi five cun long; both ends bored and fitted with gilded iron.
translations.idiomatic: Two shafts, one zhang seven chi five cun long, had gilded iron fittings at both ends.

sentences.zh: 軫長六尺二寸。

translations.literal: The frame six chi two cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The frame was six chi two cun long.

sentences.zh: 駕馬一。

translations.literal: Drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by one horse.

sentences.zh: 儀車，木質，魨明黃，高九尺五寸。

translations.literal: The ceremonial carriage: wooden, lacquered bright yellow, nine chi five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial carriage was wood lacquered bright yellow, nine chi five cun high.

sentences.zh: 穹蓋，上圓下方，高九寸。

translations.literal: Domed canopy, round above and square below, nine cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The domed canopy was round above and square below, nine cun high.

sentences.zh: 冠銀圓頂，塗金。

translations.literal: Crowned with a silver round top, gilded.

sentences.zh: 四隅系紃，明黃絨為之，屬於軫。

translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow velvet cords at the four corners tied to the frame.

sentences.zh: 明黃緞垂幨。

translations.literal: Bright yellow satin hanging curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Bright yellow satin curtains hung down.

sentences.zh: 四柱，高二尺八寸，不加繪飾，里魨淺紅。

translations.literal: Four pillars, two chi eight cun high, without added painted ornament; the interior lacquered pale red.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars stood two chi eight cun high, undecorated, with pale red lacquer inside.

sentences.zh: 黃里明黃緞幃。

translations.literal: Yellow lining, bright yellow satin curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow lining and bright yellow satin curtains.

sentences.zh: 坐具亦明黃緞為之，上綉彩鳳。

translations.literal: The seat cushion also of bright yellow satin, embroidered with colored phoenixes above.

sentences.zh: 輪徑四尺，各十有八輻。

translations.idiomatic: Wheels measured four chi in diameter, each with eighteen spokes.

sentences.zh: 轅二，長一丈五尺，鑽以鐵鋄銀，軫長五尺八寸，駕馬一。

sentences.zh: 按初制無儀車，有大儀轎，廣二尺九寸，高四尺八寸。

translations.literal: Note: in the initial system there was no ceremonial carriage; there was a great ceremonial palanquin, two chi nine cun wide, four chi eight cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Originally there was no ceremonial carriage, only a great ceremonial palanquin two chi nine cun wide and four chi eight cun high.

sentences.zh: 頂廣如儀輿。

translations.literal: The top width like the ceremonial litter.
translations.idiomatic: The top was as wide as the ceremonial litter.

sentences.zh: 頂樓八瓣，俱施黃油。

translations.literal: The top pavilion eight petals; all coated with yellow oil.
translations.idiomatic: An eight-petal top pavilion was coated throughout with yellow oil.

sentences.zh: 貼金雲鳳絛環，嵌五色寶石。

translations.literal: Gilded cloud-and-phoenix bands and rings, inset with five-colored precious stones.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded cloud-and-phoenix bands and rings were inset with gems of five colors.

sentences.zh: 黃綾為衣，上銷金鳳瀝水二層。

translations.idiomatic: Yellow gauze covered it, with two tiers of gilded phoenix drip-lines.

sentences.zh: 直橫竿各二，短扛四，肩扛倍之，撐竿二，俱硃魨。

translations.literal: Two vertical poles and two horizontal poles each; four short carrying poles; shoulder poles twice as many; two support poles—all lacquered vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: There were two vertical and two horizontal poles, four short carrying poles, twice as many shoulder poles, and two support poles—all lacquered vermilion.

sentences.zh: 轎頂飾金鳳十二，金頂鈒海馬文，嵌青、紅、藍三色寶石。

translations.literal: The palanquin top ornamented with twelve gilded phoenixes; the gilded top chased with sea-horse patterns, inset with green, red, and blue precious stones.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin top bore twelve gilded phoenixes; the gilded cap was chased with sea-horse motifs and set with green, red, and blue gems.

sentences.zh: 轎扛裝鍍金銅鳳首尾。

translations.literal: The palanquin poles fitted with gilded copper phoenix heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded copper phoenix heads and tails adorned the palanquin poles.

sentences.zh: 幰衣諸制與儀輿同。

translations.literal: Canopy garments and other specifications the same as the ceremonial litter.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy garments and other details matched the ceremonial litter.

sentences.zh: 皇太后輿車之制，與皇后同，惟繪綉加龍，故遂異其名曰龍輿、曰龍鳳車。

translations.literal: The regulations for the Empress Dowager's litters and carriages were the same as the Empress's, except that painting and embroidery added dragons; therefore their names differed—the dragon litter and the dragon-phoenix carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's litters and carriages followed the Empress's regulations, but painting and embroidery added dragons, so they were called the dragon litter and the dragon-phoenix carriage.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，皇太后六旬聖壽，皇上自暢春園躬奉慈駕入宮。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, on the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday, the Emperor personally escorted her from the Changchun Garden into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 16, for the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday, the Emperor personally escorted her from Changchun Garden into the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇太后御金輦，明黃緞綉壽字篆文。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager rode the gilded palanquin, bright yellow satin embroidered with longevity characters in seal script.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager rode a gilded palanquin draped in bright yellow satin embroidered with seal-script longevity characters.

sentences.zh: 奉輦以二十八人。

translations.literal: Twenty-eight men bore the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight bearers carried the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 二十六年、三十六年，皇太后七旬、八旬聖壽，並御是輦，自暢春園入宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth and thirty-sixth years, on the Empress Dowager's seventieth and eightieth birthdays, she likewise rode this palanquin from Changchun Garden into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On her seventieth and eightieth birthdays in the twenty-sixth and thirty-sixth years, she again rode this palanquin from Changchun Garden into the palace.

sentences.zh: 定名曰萬壽輦。

translations.literal: It was formally named the Ten-Thousand-Years Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: It was formally named the Ten-Thousand-Years Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃翟輿，木質，魨明黃，繪綉皆金翟。

translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Noble Consort's pheasant litter was wood lacquered bright yellow, with gilded pheasants in all painting and embroidery.

sentences.zh: 橫杆中為鐵鋄銀雙翟相向，翟首鋄金。

translations.idiomatic: The horizontal pole's center bore facing silver-gilt iron pheasants with gilded heads.

sentences.zh: 凡桿縱加銅鋄金翟首尾。

translations.literal: On every pole lengthwise gilded pheasant heads and tails were added.
translations.idiomatic: Every pole had gilded pheasant heads and tails added along its length.

translations.idiomatic: There were four shoulder poles.

translations.literal: The rest the same as the Empress's phoenix litter regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else matched the Empress's phoenix litter.

sentences.zh: 按初制，皇貴妃輿車，有翟車、翟轎，無儀輿、儀車之稱。

translations.literal: Note: in the initial system, the Imperial Noble Consort's litters and carriages had pheasant carriages and pheasant palanquins, without the titles ceremonial litter or ceremonial carriage.

translations.idiomatic: All was golden-yellow oiled, painted with clouds, dragons, and pheasants, and set with gems of five colors.

sentences.zh: 金黃綾衣，上銷金翟瀝水。

translations.literal: Double-eaves drip-lines, red silk lining.

translations.literal: Provincial governors and governors-general had eight litter bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors and governors-general had eight litter bearers.

sentences.zh: 司、道以下，教職以上，輿夫四人。

translations.literal: From circuit intendants down to educational officials and above, four litter bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendants down through educational officials had four litter bearers.

sentences.zh: 雜職乘馬。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous officials rode horses.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous officials rode horses.

sentences.zh: 欽差官三品以上，輿夫八人。

translations.literal: Imperial commissioners of third rank and above had eight litter bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioners of third rank and above had eight litter bearers.

sentences.zh: 武職三品仍不得用。

translations.literal: Military officials of third rank still might not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank military officials still could not use litters.

sentences.zh: 武職均乘馬。

translations.literal: Military officials all rode horses.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials all rode horses.

sentences.zh: 將軍、提督、總兵官，年逾七十不能乘馬者，奏聞請旨。

translations.literal: Generals, provincial commanders, and regional commanders who passed seventy and could not ride horses were to memorialize and await the imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Generals, provincial commanders, and regional commanders past seventy who could no longer ride horses had to memorialize and await imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 初制，凡公、侯、伯以下職官，三品以上，坐四人暗轎，鍍金裝飾，銀螭，綉帶，青幔。

translations.literal: Note: in the initial system, all officials from dukes, marquises, and earls downward of third rank and above rode enclosed litters borne by four men, with gilded ornament, silver chilong, embroidered belts, and blue curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Originally officials from dukes, marquises, and earls downward of third rank and above rode four-man enclosed litters with gilded ornament, silver chilong, embroidered belts, and blue curtains.

sentences.zh: 四品以下，坐二人暗轎，或乘車，原乘馬者聽。

translations.literal: Fourth rank and below rode two-man enclosed litters, or carriages; those who originally rode horses were permitted to continue.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and below rode two-man enclosed litters or carriages; those who had ridden horses were allowed to keep doing so.

sentences.zh: 其轎、車之制，四、五品素獅綉帶。

translations.literal: The regulations for their litters and carriages: fourth and fifth ranks had plain lion embroidered belts.
translations.idiomatic: Their litters and carriages: fourth and fifth ranks had plain lion-embroidered belts.

sentences.zh: 六品以下，素雲頭素帶，青幔。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below had plain cloud-head plain belts and blue curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below had plain cloud-head belts and blue curtains.

sentences.zh: 漢武官有坐轎者，禁如例。

translations.literal: Han military officials who rode litters were forbidden as in the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Han military officials who rode litters were forbidden under the same rules.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十五年諭：「本朝舊制，文、武滿、漢大臣，凡遇朝會皆乘馬，並不坐轎。

translations.literal: An edict in the fifteenth year of Qianlong stated: "According to our dynasty's ancient system, civil and military Manchu and Han grand ministers, whenever they attended court assemblies, all rode horses and did not ride in litters.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 15 an edict declared: "Under our dynasty's ancient custom, civil and military Manchu and Han grand ministers all rode horses to court and never used litters.

sentences.zh: 從前滿洲大臣內有坐轎者，是以降旨禁止武大臣坐轎，未禁止文大臣。

translations.literal: Formerly some Manchu grand ministers rode in litters; therefore an edict was issued forbidding military grand ministers from riding in litters, but not civil grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Some Manchu grand ministers had ridden in litters before, so an edict forbade military grand ministers from doing so but not civil ones.

sentences.zh: 今聞文大臣內務求安逸，於京師至近之地，亦皆坐轎。

translations.literal: Now it is heard that civil grand ministers, seeking ease above all, even in places very near the capital all ride in litters.
translations.idiomatic: Now civil grand ministers, bent on comfort, ride in litters even for the shortest distances within the capital.

sentences.zh: 若謂在部院行走應當坐轎，則國初部院大臣未嘗坐轎。

translations.literal: If one says that walking about the ministries and boards requires riding in a litter, then in the dynasty's founding the ministers of the ministries and boards never rode in litters.
translations.idiomatic: If going about the ministries requires a litter, the founding ministers of those boards never used one.

sentences.zh: 此由平時不勤習技業，惟求安逸之所致也。

translations.literal: This comes from not diligently practicing their skills in ordinary times, but seeking ease alone.
translations.idiomatic: This comes from neglecting their duties in ordinary times and seeking comfort alone.

sentences.zh: 滿洲大臣當思本朝舊制，遵照奉行。

translations.literal: Manchu grand ministers should reflect on our dynasty's ancient system and follow it in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu grand ministers should reflect on our dynasty's ancient custom and obey it.

sentences.zh: 嗣後文大臣內年及六旬實不能乘馬者，著照常坐轎，其餘著禁止。」

translations.literal: Henceforth among civil grand ministers, those who reach sixty and truly cannot ride horses may continue to ride in litters as before; all others are forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth civil grand ministers who reach sixty and truly cannot ride horses may still use litters; all others are forbidden."

sentences.zh: 庶民車，黑油，齊頭，平頂，皁幔。

translations.literal: Commoners' carriages: black lacquer, even front, flat top, black curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' carriages were black-lacquered, even-fronted, flat-topped, with black curtains.

sentences.zh: 轎同車制。

translations.literal: Palanquins followed the same regulations as carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquins followed the same rules as carriages.

sentences.zh: 其用雲頭者禁之。

translations.literal: The use of cloud-head motifs was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-head motifs were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 一品命婦車，黑輪、轅，皁蓋，青緣，綠幨，皁幃。

translations.literal: The first-rank titled lady's carriage: black wheels and shafts, black canopy, blue edging, green curtains, black inner curtains.
translations.idiomatic: A first-rank titled lady had black wheels and shafts, a black canopy, blue edging, green curtains, and black inner curtains.

sentences.zh: 二品命婦車，皁蓋，不緣。

translations.literal: The second-rank titled lady's carriage: black canopy, without edging.
translations.idiomatic: A second-rank titled lady had a black canopy without edging.

sentences.zh: 餘同一品命婦。

translations.literal: The rest the same as a first-rank titled lady.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else matched a first-rank titled lady.

sentences.zh: 三品命婦車，皁蓋，皁幃。

translations.literal: The third-rank titled lady's carriage: black canopy, black inner curtains.
translations.idiomatic: A third-rank titled lady had a black canopy and black inner curtains.

sentences.zh: 餘同二品命婦。

translations.literal: The rest the same as a second-rank titled lady.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else matched a second-rank titled lady.

sentences.zh: 以上輿用銀頂。

translations.literal: For the above, litters used silver tops.
translations.idiomatic: The above ranks used silver litter tops.

sentences.zh: 四品命婦車，皁蓋，青幃，輿用錫頂。

translations.literal: The fourth-rank titled lady's carriage: black canopy, blue inner curtains; the litter used a tin top.
translations.idiomatic: A fourth-rank titled lady had a black canopy and blue inner curtains, with a tin litter top.

sentences.zh: 餘同三品命婦。

translations.literal: The rest the same as a third-rank titled lady.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else matched a third-rank titled lady.

sentences.zh: 五品命婦以下車，青蓋，青幨，青幃。

translations.literal: Carriages of fifth-rank titled ladies and below: blue canopy, blue curtains, blue inner curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank titled ladies and below had blue canopies, curtains, and inner curtains.

sentences.zh: 二品以上，蓋、幃、幨用繒，餘均用布。

translations.literal: Second rank and above used silk for canopy, inner curtains, and curtains; the rest all used cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank and above used silk for canopies, inner curtains, and curtains; lower ranks used cloth.

sentences.zh: 並按初制，內大臣、都統、大學士、尚書、左都御史命婦車，青蓋，綠緣，綠幨，青幃。

translations.literal: Also per the initial system, titled ladies of inner court ministers, banner commanders, grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief had carriages with blue canopy, green edging, green curtains, and blue inner curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Originally titled ladies of inner court ministers, banner commanders, grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief had blue canopies, green edging, green curtains, and blue inner curtains.

sentences.zh: 散秩大臣、前鋒統領、步軍統領、副都統、侍郎、學士、副都御史、通政使司通政使、大理寺卿、詹事府詹事命婦車，青蓋，青幃，綠幨。

translations.literal: Titled ladies of officials without regular posts, vanguard commanders, metropolitan garrison commanders, deputy banner commanders, vice ministers, academicians, vice censor-in-chief, chief secretaries of the Office of Transmission, presidents of the Court of Judicial Review, and chancellors of the Household of the Heir Apparent had carriages with blue canopy, blue inner curtains, and green curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies of officials without regular posts, vanguard commanders, metropolitan garrison commanders, deputy banner commanders, vice ministers, academicians, vice censor-in-chief, transmission chief secretaries, judicial review presidents, and heir-apparent household chancellors had blue canopies, blue inner curtains, and green curtains.

sentences.zh: 頭等侍衛，參領，步軍總尉，王府長史，太常、太僕、光祿寺各正、少卿，通政司副使，大理寺少卿，國子監祭酒，內閣侍讀學士，翰林院讀講學士，侍讀，侍講，詹事府少詹事，庶子，諭德，洗馬，郎中，鴻臚寺卿，給事中，監察御史，輕車都尉命婦車，青蓋，青幃，青幨。

translations.literal: Titled ladies of first-class bodyguards, company commanders, metropolitan garrison captains, princely household chief stewards, chief and vice directors of the Boards of Rites, Works, and Revenue, transmission vice secretaries, judicial review vice presidents, directors of the Imperial Academy, inner court reader-academicians, Hanlin reader-lecturers, readers, lecturers, vice chancellors of the heir-apparent household, tutors, preceptors, palace stewards, bureau directors, presidents of the Court of State Ceremonial, censors, supervising secretaries, and barons had carriages with blue canopy, blue inner curtains, and blue curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies of first-class bodyguards, company commanders, garrison captains, princely chief stewards, ritual, works, and revenue directors, transmission vice secretaries, judicial review vice presidents, academy directors, inner court reader-academicians, Hanlin reader-lecturers, readers, lecturers, heir-apparent vice chancellors, tutors, preceptors, palace stewards, bureau directors, state ceremonial presidents, censors, supervising secretaries, and barons had blue canopies, blue inner curtains, and blue curtains.

sentences.zh: 閒散宗室、二等侍衛、佐領、貝勒長史、欽天監監正、內閣侍讀、國子監司業、鴻臚寺少卿、通政使司參議、詹事府中允、員外郎、步軍副尉、騎都尉命婦車，青蓋，藍幃，青幨。

translations.literal: Titled ladies of idle banner nobles, second-class bodyguards, assistant commanders, beile household chief stewards, directors of the Directorate of Astronomy, inner court readers, academy vice directors, state ceremonial vice presidents, transmission counselors, heir-apparent household middle attendants, bureau vice directors, garrison lieutenants, and commanders had carriages with blue canopy, indigo inner curtains, and blue curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies of idle banner nobles, second-class bodyguards, assistant commanders, beile chief stewards, astronomy directors, inner court readers, academy vice directors, state ceremonial vice presidents, transmission counselors, heir-apparent middle attendants, bureau vice directors, garrison lieutenants, and commanders had blue canopies, indigo inner curtains, and blue curtains.

sentences.zh: 三等侍衛、雲騎尉、五品以下官命婦車，藍蓋，藍幃，青幨。

translations.literal: Titled ladies of third-class bodyguards, cloud-cavalry commanders, and officials of fifth rank and below had carriages with indigo canopy, indigo inner curtains, and blue curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies of third-class bodyguards, cloud-cavalry commanders, and officials of fifth rank and below had indigo canopies and inner curtains with blue curtains.
